elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt to a nonzero prescaler, keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue the supported START command cmd=0001 on a clock-enable opportunity, then continue clocking until the command completes or aborts.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: during the active START sequence, scl_oen follows the command-specific bit-level SCL phases: it is released high for the required START high phase and then drives SCL low before the sequence completes and cmd_ack pulses.
elements.check_method: Use the divider and FSM reference model to identify command acceptance and each timed phase; sample registered scl_oen after every posedge and compare its phase sequence and ordering against the model, requiring no unexpected fixed value throughout the active sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive cmd=0000 (NOP), then drive an unsupported 4-bit command such as cmd=0011 while the bus inputs remain released high; hold each command for multiple clocks without issuing a supported command.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise side of shows: because no enabled supported START, STOP, READ, or WRITE sequence is active, scl_oen remains in its idle released state and does not follow a command-specific timed SCL high/low phase sequence; no cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle and scl_oen over all driven-command clocks; compare against the idle reference model and assert that scl_oen remains released, no active command phase is entered, and cmd_ack stays low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue cmd=START (0001) on a clock-enable opportunity, and maintain the command until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0001: scl_oen and sda_oen follow the START timed sequence: both initially released, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released high, then SCL is driven low while the START sequence completes; the sequence terminates with cmd_ack and the output enables return to the command's idle state.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate command/FSM reference model and compare sampled scl_oen and sda_oen after each posedge from command acceptance through cmd_ack, checking phase ordering and open-drain polarity.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue cmd=STOP (0010) on a clock-enable opportunity, and maintain the command until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0001: scl_oen and sda_oen follow the STOP timed sequence: SDA is driven low, SCL is released high, and SDA is then released while SCL is high; the sequence terminates with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered output-enable trace against a reference STOP sequence at every enabled timing phase, verifying SDA-low, SCL-release, SDA-release ordering and completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0, keep the externally resolved SDA and SCL lines high unless driven by the DUT, and maintain the command until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0001: during the WRITE sequence sda_oen is asserted low to drive SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, then scl_oen drives SCL low for completion; the timed sequence ends with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the open-drain bus model and a cycle-accurate WRITE reference model to compare sda_oen and scl_oen during low, released-high, and final-low phases, including exact phase ordering.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, keep the externally resolved SDA and SCL lines high, and maintain the command until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0001: during the WRITE sequence sda_oen remains released high for din=1, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, then drives SCL low for completion; the timed sequence ends with cmd_ack without an arbitration abort when SDA remains high.
elements.check_method: Compare the output-enable trace to the WRITE-din=1 reference model, checking that SDA is released rather than driven low and that the SCL release/high/final-low phases occur in order.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue cmd=READ (1000), drive sda_i high during the read sample window, and maintain the command and bus inputs until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0001: sda_oen is released for the entire read bit, scl_oen releases SCL for the timed read window, then drives SCL low; the sequence ends with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Correlate filtered SCL timing and the read-window probe with the registered scl_oen/sda_oen trace, comparing each phase and its duration against the reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset and while idle with ena=1, issue cmd=0000 and then each unsupported 4-bit encoding other than 0001, 0010, 0100, and 1000 for at least one enabled timing opportunity, with scl_i and sda_i high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of REQ-0001: scl_oen and sda_oen do not follow any command-dependent SCL/SDA control sequence; the FSM remains idle, no command phase is entered, and no cmd_ack is produced.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle and command-sequence probes while checking that no non-idle output-enable phase occurs and that cmd_ack remains low for every unsupported encoding.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, then issue cmd=START on an enabled timing tick while modeling the released bus as high.
elements.expected_response: The controller generates a valid START sequence: SDA is released initially, then sda_oen drives SDA low while SCL is high, followed by scl_oen driving SCL low. cmd_ack pulses once when the sequence completes. This is the holding side of the busy observation: busy rises when the filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high is detected.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for clk_en, input filtering, FSM phases, and registered outputs; assert the ordered scl_oen/sda_oen phases, one-clock cmd_ack pulse, and busy rising at the filtered START detection event.

elements.stimulus: First establish busy with a valid START, then issue cmd=STOP with ena=1 while the filtered bus is high and allow all timing ticks and any required SCL release wait to occur.
elements.expected_response: The controller drives SDA low, releases SCL high, then releases SDA while SCL is high to form a STOP condition, and pulses cmd_ack once. This is the holding side of the busy observation: busy clears when the filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high is detected.
elements.check_method: Compare registered open-drain enables and cmd_ack against a protocol reference model, and assert that busy clears only at the modeled filtered STOP detection edge.

elements.stimulus: While the controller is idle with busy low, hold filtered SCL high and inject SDA and SCL raw-line pulses shorter than the configured synchronization/filter sampling interval, returning both lines high before a majority-filtered transition can form.
elements.expected_response: The synchronizers and majority filter process the inputs without producing a filtered START or STOP. This is the contrasting, non-holding side of the busy observation: busy remains unchanged because no corresponding filtered START or STOP transition occurs; no command completion or arbitration-loss indication is generated.
elements.check_method: Drive raw inputs with pulse widths below the modeled filter qualification time and compare filter histories, start_condition/stop_condition probes, busy, cmd_ack, and al against the reference model.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue a single-bit WRITE command with din=0, then provide a high external bus response during the released SCL phase.
elements.expected_response: The controller drives SDA low by asserting sda_oen=0, releases SCL for the high phase, pulls SCL low again, returns to idle, and pulses cmd_ack once. No arbitration loss is reported because a low SDA value is expected for din=0.
elements.check_method: Check the WRITE state sequence and active-low output-enable polarity against a reference model; assert al remains low and cmd_ack is exactly one clock.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, issue a single-bit WRITE command with din=1; during the released-high SCL phase externally hold SDA low, while allowing filtered SCL to complete the high phase.
elements.expected_response: The controller releases SDA for din=1, detects arbitration loss from filtered SDA low during the WRITE high phase, asserts sticky al, aborts the command without cmd_ack, returns the FSM to idle, and releases both SDA and SCL output enables.
elements.check_method: Use the arbitration reference model at the write_stable_high_phase and arbitration_checking probes; assert al becomes high, cmd_ack stays low for the aborted command, and both output enables are released after abort.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue a READ command; first drive filtered SDA low through the read sample window and complete a filtered SCL rising edge, then repeat the transaction with filtered SDA high.
elements.expected_response: For each transaction the controller releases SDA, releases SCL for the read window, captures the filtered SDA value into dout on the filtered SCL rising edge, pulls SCL low, and emits one cmd_ack pulse. dout is 0 in the first transaction and 1 in the second.
elements.check_method: Run both data trials against a filtered-input and FSM reference model; sample dout after the registered filtered_scl_rise update and assert the corresponding output-enable phase and cmd_ack timing.

elements.stimulus: Issue a START, WRITE, or READ command with ena=1, release SCL through a high phase, and hold scl_i low externally so that filtered SCL remains low for several expected timing ticks; then release scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: The controller enters slave-wait behavior, pauses the timing counter and FSM progression while filtered SCL is low, and resumes the command only after filtered SCL becomes high. The command then completes with the normal protocol phase ordering and cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Monitor slave_wait, clk_en_tick, FSM probes, output enables, and cmd_ack; compare elapsed cycles and resumption point with a reference model that suppresses ticks during stretching.

elements.stimulus: During a command high phase in which the DUT has released SCL, drive filtered SCL high and then force an external SCL falling transition, maintaining the external low level long enough for synchronization and filtering.
elements.expected_response: The controller detects the multi-master SCL falling event, asserts the synchronization event, reloads its timing counter, restarts the low-period timing, and does not advance the high-phase FSM as if it had independently controlled the original clock.
elements.check_method: Correlate scl_sync_event, clk_en_tick, counter behavior, filtered SCL history, FSM probes, and output enables with a multi-master synchronization reference model.

elements.stimulus: Run enabled command and external-bus activity tests with clk_cnt values 0, 1, and a larger prescaler value, including stable and glitching scl_i/sda_i inputs.
elements.expected_response: For clk_cnt=0, filtering samples at the safe minimum interval and clk_en occurs on every enabled clock without a stuck divider. For clk_cnt=1 and larger values, timing and filter samples follow the corresponding prescaled intervals. Commands still preserve protocol ordering and produce completion unless blocked by intentional stretching or arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Compare divider reload/decrement, clk_en_tick, filter_sample_event, filtered values, command phase progression, and output pulses against a parameterized cycle-accurate reference model for all three prescaler classes.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, then issue a valid START command. After command acceptance, allow the START sequence to reach its SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase and its subsequent SCL-low phase, sampling outputs after every posedge.
elements.expected_response: This is the drive-low side of the observed behavior: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, scl_oen is 1 while SCL is released and becomes 0 during the SCL-low phase, and sda_oen becomes 0 during the SDA-low phase. The external open-drain line model therefore drives a selected line low only when its corresponding enable is 0.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0; compare scl_oen and sda_oen against a reference model of the START output phases and compute each external line as low when its enable is 0, otherwise released/high.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, leave ena=1 with no command pending, and sample the outputs over multiple posedges. Then issue a STOP command after the controller is active and sample the final STOP phase in which both lines are released.
elements.expected_response: This is the release side of the observed behavior: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, while scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1 in the idle and final STOP-release phases. The external open-drain line model therefore releases both lines rather than actively driving them low.
elements.check_method: At every sampled posedge, assert both drive outputs are 0 and compare both output enables with the idle/STOP reference model; verify that enable value 1 corresponds to released external lines and value 0, when present during STOP sequencing, corresponds to an active low drive.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue START and, after completion, issue WRITE with din=0 while the external SCL and SDA participants do not drive the lines low.
elements.expected_response: During every SCL-low or SDA-low phase, the corresponding output enable is 0: scl_oen=0 when SCL is driven low and sda_oen=0 when SDA is driven low. The constant drive outputs scl_o and sda remain 0 at every observation, including during phases where the lines are released.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_o, sda_o, scl_oen, and sda_oen after each settled posedge and compare against a transaction reference model; cover START and WRITE(din=0) drive phases and assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 for the entire run.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue START and then READ, allowing the external bus to remain released high and return SDA=1 during the read window.
elements.expected_response: During every SCL-high or SDA-high/released phase, the corresponding output enable is 1: scl_oen=1 when SCL is released and sda_oen=1 when SDA is released. The constant drive outputs scl_o and sda remain 0 at every observation, including during phases where the lines are driven low.
elements.check_method: Sample the four outputs after each settled posedge and compare against a transaction reference model; cover START release phases and the READ release/sample window, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 throughout, and assert the enable polarity is 1 for each released line.

elements.stimulus: Release the external SCL and SDA drivers so both bus lines are high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command, and wait through the START sequence until the FSM reaches the phase that drives SDA low and SCL low.
elements.expected_response: During the stable low-drive phase, scl_oen=0 and sda_oen=0; the resolved SCL and SDA lines are pulled low. This is the low side of the requirement's shows statement for both ports.
elements.check_method: At posedges after registered outputs settle, assert scl_o=0 and sda_o=0, scl_oen=0 and sda_oen=0, and sample resolved SCL/SDA nets with external drivers released; compare both nets against 0 for the entire stable enable interval.

elements.stimulus: Release the external SCL and SDA drivers so both pull-ups can raise the bus, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command, and observe the initial START-sequence phase before the controller pulls SDA low.
elements.expected_response: During the stable release phase, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1; the resolved SCL and SDA lines are high due to the external pull-ups. This is the high-release side of the requirement's shows statement for both ports.
elements.check_method: At posedges after registered outputs settle, assert scl_o=0 and sda_o=0, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, and sample resolved SCL/SDA nets with external drivers released; compare both nets against 1 for the entire stable enable interval.

elements.stimulus: Release the external SCL and SDA drivers, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a WRITE command with din=0, and wait until the WRITE data phase is active.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE data phase drives SDA low with sda_oen=0, so the resolved SDA line is low. SCL remains controlled by its current phase; this scenario specifically checks the low-drive side of the SDA shows statement.
elements.check_method: At the stable WRITE data phase, assert sda_o=0 and sda_oen=0, sample the resolved SDA net with no external low driver, and compare it against 0 until sda_oen changes.

elements.stimulus: Release the external SCL and SDA drivers, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and wait until the WRITE data phase is active before the SCL high phase.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE data phase releases SDA with sda_oen=1, allowing the external pull-up to make the resolved SDA line high. This is the high-release side of the SDA shows statement.
elements.check_method: At the stable WRITE data phase, assert sda_o=0 and sda_oen=1, sample the resolved SDA net with no external low driver, and compare it against 1 until sda_oen changes.

elements.stimulus: Instantiate i2c_master_bit_ctrl in the overall I2C master test harness at the Bit Command Controller integration point, connect all declared ports by name, and elaborate the design.
elements.expected_response: The design elaborates successfully with i2c_master_bit_ctrl present at the Bit Command Controller hierarchy location, with all specified ports bound to the corresponding architecture signals and no extra or missing module ports.
elements.check_method: Use compilation and elaboration logs plus a post-elaboration hierarchy and port-binding check to confirm the module instance identity, hierarchy placement, and exact interface binding.

elements.stimulus: After reset, release both external bus lines high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then present cmd=START on a posedge and continue clocking until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case side of shows: during the active START sequence, scl_oen and sda_oen exhibit the commanded SCL/SDA phases: both lines are initially released, SDA is driven low while SCL is released high, and SCL is subsequently driven low before command completion. scl_o and sda remain constant 0 throughout.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to compare sampled registered scl_oen and sda_oen after each posedge from command acceptance through cmd_ack, checking phase ordering and final idle release; assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 in every sampled cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, release SCL and SDA, set din=0, issue cmd=WRITE, and clock until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case side of shows: the commanded WRITE operation drives SDA low by setting sda_oen=0 for the data phase, releases SCL with scl_oen=1 for the high phase, then drives SCL low with scl_oen=0 before returning idle. scl_o and sda remain constant 0.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed registered output-enable waveform against a reference WRITE(din=0) model, checking that SDA is owned low before and during the SCL high phase and that both phase transitions occur in the required order; continuously check scl_o==0 and sda_o==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, release SCL and SDA, set din=1, issue cmd=WRITE, and clock until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case side of shows: the commanded WRITE operation releases SDA by setting sda_oen=1 for the data phase, releases SCL with scl_oen=1 for the high phase, then drives SCL low with scl_oen=0 before returning idle. scl_o and sda remain constant 0.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed registered output-enable waveform against a reference WRITE(din=1) model and verify that sda_oen differs from the din=0 case during the data phase while the SCL phase sequence remains correct; continuously check scl_o==0 and sda_o==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, release SCL and SDA, issue cmd=READ, provide a stable external SDA value, and clock until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case side of shows: the commanded READ operation keeps SDA released with sda_oen=1, releases SCL with scl_oen=1 for the read window, and then drives SCL low with scl_oen=0 before completion. scl_o and sda remain constant 0.
elements.check_method: Compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen at each posedge against a reference READ waveform, checking SDA release throughout the sample window and the ordered SCL release/drive-low phases; continuously check scl_o==0 and sda_o==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue START and allow it to complete, then issue STOP while the bus is otherwise released and clock until the STOP cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case side of shows: the commanded STOP operation drives SDA low with sda_oen=0, releases SCL with scl_oen=1, then releases SDA with sda_oen=1 while SCL remains released, creating the STOP line sequence. scl_o and sda remain constant 0.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered output-enable sequence from STOP acceptance through cmd_ack against a reference STOP model, checking the SDA-low, SCL-release, SDA-release ordering and final released state; continuously check scl_o==0 and sda_o==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, first present cmd=NOP and then an unsupported 4-bit command value with ena=1; separately hold a supported cmd=START while ena=0 for multiple enabled-clock intervals.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise-case side of shows: no command-dependent SCL or SDA output-enable sequence occurs for NOP, unsupported commands, or a disabled core. scl_oen and sda_oen remain at the idle released value 1, with no command completion, while scl_o and sda remain constant 0.
elements.check_method: Assert that scl_oen and sda_oen do not change from their reset/idle values and that no active-command waveform or cmd_ack occurs during each no-operation interval; compare all four outputs with the idle reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, present cmd=START, keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, and provide clk_cnt and enabled clock cycles until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the active START bit-level sequence, scl_oen and sda_oen change from their idle released states to generate the START waveform: SDA is driven low while SCL is released high, followed by SCL being driven low; cmd_ack then pulses once.
elements.check_method: Trace scl_oen and sda_oen on each settled posedge from command acceptance through cmd_ack, and compare the observed phase ordering against an I2C START reference model.

elements.stimulus: After a START has made the controller busy, set ena=1 and present cmd=STOP; keep the bus externally released high and provide enabled clock cycles until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the active STOP bit-level sequence, sda_oen drives SDA low, scl_oen releases SCL high, and sda_oen then releases SDA high while SCL is high; cmd_ack pulses once after the sequence.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and sda_oen with a temporal checker that requires the STOP phase sequence and completion pulse, allowing latency variation from the timing counter.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, present cmd=WRITE with din=0, hold scl_i and sda_i high unless the DUT drives them low, and run enabled clock cycles through command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the active WRITE bit-level sequence, sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, then drives SCL low again; cmd_ack pulses once.
elements.check_method: Compare the sampled scl_oen and sda_oen waveform against a WRITE(din=0) reference model, checking low/high/low SCL phase ordering and the SDA output-enable polarity.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, present cmd=WRITE with din=1, keep the external bus released high, and run enabled clock cycles through command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the active WRITE bit-level sequence, sda_oen releases SDA for din=1, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, then drives SCL low; cmd_ack pulses once without arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Use a waveform checker and reference model to verify SDA release, SCL release-then-drive-low ordering, and one completion pulse with al remaining low.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, present cmd=READ, externally provide sda_i=0 and then sda_i=1 during separate read transactions while providing scl_i high for the read window and enabled clock cycles until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during each active READ bit-level sequence, sda_oen remains released, scl_oen releases SCL for the read window and later drives it low, and cmd_ack pulses once; the output-enable waveform is independent of the returned data bit.
elements.check_method: Run a READ reference model against scl_oen and sda_oen, checking SDA remains released and the SCL high/low phase ordering for both returned data values.

elements.stimulus: From idle, set ena=1 and present cmd=NOP for multiple enabled clock cycles; repeat with each unsupported 4-bit cmd value other than 0000, 0001, 0010, 0100, and 1000.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: no supported bit-level command is executed, so scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the unrelated idle released state and do not change between driven-low and released-high states; no cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Assert that the output enables remain at their idle values for the entire stimulus window and that cmd_ack remains low, contrasting this trace with the active-command waveform requirements.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate i2c_master_bit_ctrl with a testbench using named connections for input ports clk, rst, nReset, and ena; drive clk with a periodic waveform, toggle rst synchronously high on a rising edge, assert and deassert nReset asynchronously, and drive ena low and high.
elements.expected_response: Requirement holding: compilation and elaboration succeed, and all four named connections bind as input ports without port-not-found, direction, or width errors.
elements.check_method: Use the simulator/compiler exit status and elaboration diagnostics, plus an interface assertion or VPI/HDL reflection check that clk, rst, nReset, and ena exist with input direction and one-bit width.

elements.stimulus: Run a negative compile job against a mutated i2c_master_bit_ctrl declaration in which at least one of clk, rst, nReset, or ena is omitted or is declared with the wrong direction, while the testbench still instantiates and connects all four required named ports.
elements.expected_response: Requirement not holding: compilation or elaboration fails with a diagnostic identifying the unavailable or incompatible required port; the DUT must not produce an elaborated design that silently accepts the incomplete interface.
elements.check_method: Require a nonzero compiler/elaborator exit status and match diagnostics against the missing-port, invalid-port, direction, or width mismatch; reject a successful elaboration.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena high and execute the same supported command twice on an otherwise released, unstretched bus, first with clk_cnt=16'h0001 and then with clk_cnt=16'h0010. Record the clock count from command acceptance to the cmd_ack pulse for each execution.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: cmd_ack is asserted as exactly one clock pulse for both executions, and the execution using clk_cnt=16'h0010 completes later than the execution using clk_cnt=16'h0001, consistently with the larger prescale value.
elements.check_method: Use a scoreboard/reference timing model for enabled divider expiration and command phase advancement. Detect the single-cycle cmd_ack pulse and compare measured acceptance-to-ack latency between the two clk_cnt settings; require the larger setting to produce the expected longer latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, execute the same supported command with ena high on a released, unstretched bus using clk_cnt=16'h0000 and then clk_cnt=16'hFFFF. Observe cmd_ack and record completion latency for each run.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows at the prescale boundaries: clk_cnt=0 must still produce a one-clock cmd_ack completion without a stuck divider, while clk_cnt=16'hFFFF must produce a substantially longer completion latency. Contrasting non-holding side: unchanged latency between these settings, or absence of the required one-clock completion pulse, demonstrates that clk_cnt is not functioning as the clock prescale value.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack pulse existence and width against a reference model that treats clk_cnt=0 as an enabled tick on every enabled clock and models the maximum reload interval for 16'hFFFF. Fail if either run lacks exactly one pulse or if the measured latency does not differ as predicted.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate i2c_master_bit_ctrl with its declared port list and bind an interface checker that queries cmd, cmd_ack, busy, and al declarations.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: cmd is present as a 4-bit input port, and cmd_ack, busy, and al are each present as one-bit output ports.
elements.check_method: Use simulator or RTL compile-time reflection/interface binding and fail the test if any named port is absent, has the wrong width, or has the wrong direction.

elements.stimulus: Run the same elaboration-time interface checker against mutation variants in which cmd_ack, busy, or al is absent, is declared as an input, or has a width other than one; also mutate cmd to a non-4-bit or non-input declaration.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case of shows: the checker rejects elaboration or reports a structural interface mismatch for each absent, incorrectly directed, or incorrectly sized port.
elements.check_method: Compile/elaborate each mutated DUT variant and compare diagnostics or checker assertions against the expected structural failure; require rejection for every mutation.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate the DUT, then inspect its module port metadata for din, dout, scl_i, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_i, sda_o, and sda_oen.
elements.expected_response: The interface shows din, scl_i, and sda_i as one-bit input ports, and dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen as one-bit output ports. This is the 'shows' side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use elaborated-design reflection or a Verilog interface/lint checker to compare every listed port name, direction, and width against the required declaration; record a passing interface-compliance check.

elements.stimulus: Run the same interface checker against negative-control DUT variants in which one listed port is absent, has the wrong direction, or is changed from one bit to a multi-bit width, including a variant for each affected port category.
elements.expected_response: The checker identifies the altered port as noncompliant and rejects the interface: for dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, or sda_oen it reports the 'otherwise' case if the port is absent, an input, or not one bit; similarly it reports noncompliance if din, scl_i, or sda_i is not a one-bit input. This is the non-'shows' side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use mutation testing with expected-failure assertions from elaboration or lint diagnostics, verifying that every absent, misdirected, or incorrectly sized port is detected and cannot pass the interface contract.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a testbench instance of i2c_master_bit_ctrl connected to all declared input ports: clk, rst, nReset, ena, clk_cnt[15:0], cmd[3:0], din, scl_i, and sda_i; drive legal values on every input.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of the port-introduction distinction: elaboration succeeds, every named input port is accepted with the specified direction and width, and the DUT produces its declared outputs without an interface error.
elements.check_method: Use compilation/elaboration status plus a structural interface assertion checking exact port names, directions, and widths against the contract; classify successful elaboration as the introduced-port case.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a negative interface harness that instantiates i2c_master_bit_ctrl while omitting one required input connection, such as nReset, or referring to a nonexistent input name in its place.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of the port-introduction distinction: compilation or elaboration fails with a missing-port or unknown-port diagnostic; the DUT must not be accepted as an instance lacking the introduced input port.
elements.check_method: Run the negative compile as an expected-failure test and match the tool diagnostic against the missing or unknown port; fail the test if elaboration succeeds.

elements.stimulus: Apply a valid reset, then set nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=1, and issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 while the external SCL and SDA lines are released high. Continue clocking clk until the command reaches its terminal completion phase, then provide successive rising and falling edges of clk around the completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack remains low before completion, asserts for exactly one clk cycle when the WRITE completes, and deasserts on the next rising edge. Its assertion and deassertion occur only on rising edges of clk.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked scoreboard/reference model to predict command completion. Sample cmd_ack after each rising edge and at intervening falling edges; require exactly one high sample on a rising edge, low at all other samples, and no asynchronous transition between rising edges.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and leave the module idle with ena=0 and cmd=NOP. Between successive rising edges of clk, toggle cmd among supported and unsupported encodings and toggle din, scl_i, and sda_i; observe cmd_ack at falling edges and immediately before and after each input transition. Do not allow a command to reach a terminal completion phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: cmd_ack remains low throughout the idle, non-completion interval and does not assert or change asynchronously, at falling edges, or in response to input transitions unrelated to a rising edge of clk.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack samples taken before and after every between-clock stimulus transition and at every falling edge against a reference model with no command completion; require it to remain 0 until a future clk-rising-edge completion, which is absent in this scenario.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena high, provide a released-high I2C bus and a valid clk_cnt, then issue a supported WRITE command with din=0. Continue clocking until the command reaches its completion event.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: cmd_ack changes only immediately after a rising edge of clk, is asserted for exactly one clock interval, and remains unchanged between rising edges.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block or post-NBA monitor to sample cmd_ack at every posedge clk and continuously between edges; compare the observed transition timestamp and pulse width against a reference model of the command sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a supported READ command with ena high, vary the external SDA value and allow any required SCL stretching, then monitor cmd_ack from command acceptance through completion, including the intervals immediately before and after the completion edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise side: cmd_ack must not assert, deassert, or pulse at any time between rising edges of clk or without a rising-edge boundary. Any such transition is evidence that the synchronous-update requirement does not hold and is a failure.
elements.check_method: Run an assertion that cmd_ack is stable throughout every open interval between consecutive rising edges of clk, while separately checking that any completion pulse begins and ends on clock boundaries; record any mid-cycle transition as a failure.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and both external bus lines released high, issue a valid START command and allow the FSM to enter its active sequence. Then assert rst=1 before a rising edge of clk and hold it through that edge.
elements.expected_response: At the rising edge with rst asserted, the synchronous reset takes effect: the command FSM returns to idle, counters and filtered-input state are reset, cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, dout=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. No command-progress output remains from the interrupted START sequence.
elements.check_method: Sample registered outputs and the in_idle probe immediately after the reset posedge; compare against the reset reference model and assert cmd_ack==0, busy==0, al==0, dout==0, scl_oen==1, sda_oen==1, and in_idle==1.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset deasserted and rst=0. With ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and the external bus released high, issue a valid START command and wait until the FSM is in the START sequence. At a subsequent rising edge of clk, continue driving rst=0 and the command inputs and bus conditions normally.
elements.expected_response: Because rst is not asserted, the module follows ordinary command behavior rather than resetting: the FSM remains active in the START sequence or advances according to its normal timing, and the output enables reflect the START phase (including sda_oen=0 when SDA is pulled low) rather than both reset idle values scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1. Status and data outputs are not forcibly cleared by that clock edge.
elements.check_method: At the selected non-reset posedge, compare outputs and in_start_sequence against the normal-operation reference model; specifically verify the FSM is not forced to idle and that the active START output phase is retained/advanced, distinguishing it from the reset response.

elements.stimulus: Deassert nReset high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a valid WRITE command with din=0, and wait until the controller is active with scl_oen=0. Between two rising edges of clk, transition nReset low and keep clk stopped until after observing the output.
elements.expected_response: scl_oen changes asynchronously to 1 before the next rising edge of clk, indicating the reset idle value immediately without waiting for clk; this is the reset-asserted side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: At the falling transition of nReset, sample scl_oen before any subsequent clk rising edge and compare it against 1'b1; assert that the transition is observed without a clock event.

elements.stimulus: Deassert nReset high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a valid WRITE command with din=0, and wait until the controller is active with scl_oen=0. Keep nReset high and observe scl_oen across an interval between two rising edges of clk without changing other inputs.
elements.expected_response: scl_oen retains its active command-phase value of 0 between clock edges and does not asynchronously change to the reset idle value; this is the nReset-deasserted otherwise side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen immediately before and after a clock-free interval while nReset remains high; compare both samples and require scl_oen to remain 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus released and the FSM idle, set ena=1, present the supported START command, and maintain ena=1 until the START sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of shows: because ena is the core enable and is high, the START command is accepted and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock cycle at command completion.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on each settled posedge of clk; compare against a command-completion reference model and require exactly one high cycle following acceptance, with cmd_ack low on all other cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the FSM idle, set ena=0, present the same supported START command while keeping ena=0 for the entire attempted command interval, then return cmd to NOP.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting side of shows: because ena is low, the command is not accepted and cmd_ack remains low; no command-complete pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack and the idle probe on each settled posedge of clk; require cmd_ack to remain 0 throughout the ena-low interval and verify that no command-completion event is reported.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to a nonzero value, keep the bus released, issue a supported WRITE command with ena high, then drive ena low after the WRITE sequence has started and before its terminal phase. Hold ena low for several clk_en intervals, then drive ena high and provide normal SCL high and low phases.
elements.expected_response: While ena is low, normal timing progression is gated: the active WRITE phase and timing/filter progression hold, and cmd_ack remains low; this is the ena-disabled side of the specified behavior. After ena returns high, the command resumes and cmd_ack produces exactly one completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the in_write_sequence, clk_en_tick, and in_idle probes with a cycle-accurate reference model. Assert that no command phase or cmd_ack transition occurs during the ena-low interval, then compare the resumed phase ordering and one-cycle cmd_ack pulse after re-enabling.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same supported WRITE transaction and bus response with ena held high continuously from command acceptance through the terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: With ena high, normal timing is not gated: the WRITE sequence advances through its phases and cmd_ack pulses when the command reaches its terminal phase; this is the contrasting enabled side of the specified behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack latency and in_write_sequence-to-in_idle transitions against the enabled reference-model schedule, and verify that the pulse is one clock wide and occurs without an ena-induced pause.

elements.stimulus: Initialize busy low with filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high. Set clk_cnt to 4, hold ena low, and drive the external bus to a stable START condition by holding SCL high and SDA low for enough clocks to exceed the synchronizer and filter intervals. Then drive ena high while maintaining the same bus levels.
elements.expected_response: While ena is low, input-filter progression and START detection are gated, so busy remains low and no START-driven status change occurs; this is the ena-disabled side of the specified behavior. After ena is driven high, filtering progresses, the stable START is detected, and busy sets.
elements.check_method: Use filter_sample_event and start_condition probes and sample busy after settled posedges. Assert no filter samples or start_condition-driven busy transition during the ena-low interval, then require busy to assert after enable according to the synchronizer/filter reference model.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same initial bus state, clk_cnt value, and stable filtered-eligible START transition, but hold ena high continuously.
elements.expected_response: With ena high, input-filter operation is not gated: the stable START is detected and busy sets; this is the contrasting enabled side of the specified behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare filter_sample_event and start_condition timing and the resulting busy assertion against the enabled reference model, requiring busy to set after the expected filtered transition.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 4, hold nReset high, provide a released-high bus, issue a supported START command with ena high until the command is accepted, then drive ena low before the START terminal phase and hold it low for at least 16 rising edges.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low side of the observed behavior: cmd_ack remains low throughout the ena-low interval and the START completion is postponed; no normal bit-timing progression or command-complete pulse occurs while ena is low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after ena falls, compare registered cmd_ack against 0 and assert that no pulse occurs during the disabled interval. After ena is returned high, use a divider/filter-aware reference model to verify that completion occurs only after timing resumes and that cmd_ack is a single-cycle pulse.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 4, hold nReset high, provide a released-high bus, issue the same supported START command with ena held high from acceptance through the terminal phase, and continue clocking until completion.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high contrasting side of the observed behavior: when ena remains high, cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock cycle when the command reaches its terminal phase rather than being postponed.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model with clk_cnt and filter timing to predict the variable terminal cycle; compare cmd_ack to a one-cycle pulse at that cycle and 0 on all other sampled cycles, and contrast its timing with TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, cmd=START, and provide a released-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Run until the START command completes, with no reset, clock stretching, or arbitration loss. Record the intervening SCL/SDA output-enable timing and cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observation: clk_cnt is accepted as a 16-bit prescale value, and the START sequence advances using the defined zero-prescaler behavior, producing enabled timing on every enabled clock without a stuck divider. cmd_ack is a one-clock completion pulse at the resulting zero-prescaler latency.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for zero-prescaler divider behavior and compare scl_oen, sda_oen, phase timing, and the one-cycle cmd_ack pulse against the model. Compare the recorded latency with the otherwise identical maximum-prescaler trial; failure to differ as predicted indicates the otherwise behavior that timing is independent of clk_cnt.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=16'hFFFF, cmd=START, and provide the same released-high bus conditions as the zero-prescaler trial: scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, with no reset, clock stretching, or arbitration loss. Run until the START command completes and record the intervening SCL/SDA output-enable timing and cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observation: clk_cnt is accepted across its full 16-bit range, and the maximum prescale value produces the corresponding longer timing intervals before START phase advancement and cmd_ack. cmd_ack remains a one-clock completion pulse. The latency and phase intervals must differ from the otherwise identical clk_cnt=0 trial as predicted by the prescale model; the otherwise side, timing independent of clk_cnt or inconsistent use of the value, is a failure.
elements.check_method: Compare the DUT waveform and cmd_ack latency with a reference model using clk_cnt=16'hFFFF, then perform a paired differential comparison against TP-0000 with identical command and bus inputs. Check that the maximum-prescaler trial has the model-predicted longer intervals and distinct completion latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt=16'd3 and ena=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, then issue cmd=START while the FSM is idle. Continue clocking until the START sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: Requirement holds: the divider loads/reloads from clk_cnt and produces clk_en_tick events at the reference-model-prescribed expiration interval. The START command is accepted on a clk_en_tick, the FSM advances through the START sequence only on subsequent clk_en_tick events, and the command eventually completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider reference model seeded with clk_cnt=3. Compare every observed clk_en_tick probe event with the model, and assert that in_start_sequence changes only on cycles with clk_en_tick; check that cmd_ack occurs after the expected modeled sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt=16'd0 and ena=1, keep the bus released high, then issue cmd=START while the FSM is idle and continue clocking through the command.
elements.expected_response: Requirement holds at the zero prescale boundary: clk_en_tick is generated on every enabled clock according to the defined zero-reload behavior, the START command is accepted without a stuck divider, and the bit-level FSM advances on successive enabled ticks until cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Compare clk_en_tick against a reference model treating clk_cnt=0 as an every-enabled-clock tick. Assert that the FSM progresses through in_start_sequence and that no interval contains a stalled divider or missing tick while ena remains high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt=16'd3 and ena=0, keep the bus released high, and present cmd=START for multiple clock cycles; then toggle ena=1 while leaving the command asserted.
elements.expected_response: Requirement does not hold while ena is low: no clk_en_tick events occur, the divider is reloaded or timing progression is disabled, the FSM remains idle, and no cmd_ack is produced. Once ena becomes high, divider ticks resume and the still-present valid command may then be accepted on a generated clk_en_tick.
elements.check_method: During the ena=0 interval, assert that clk_en_tick, in_start_sequence, and cmd_ack remain inactive and in_idle remains asserted. After ena rises, compare tick timing with the clk_cnt=3 reference model and verify command acceptance only on a subsequent clk_en_tick.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, keep ena high and the bus idle with SCL high and SDA high, set clk_cnt=0, then drive SDA low and hold it stable while continuing enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: filter_cnt samples on every enabled clock because floor(clk_cnt/4)=0; after the modeled synchronizer and majority-filter latency, the filtered SDA high-to-low transition is detected and busy rises. The measured busy latency must match the reference model for sampling every enabled clock.
elements.check_method: Reference-model the two-stage input synchronization, every-enabled-clock filter sampling, three-sample majority, and START detection; compare the predicted filtered transition and busy assertion cycle with the observed busy output, allowing only the documented registered-output latency.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, keep ena high and the bus idle with SCL high and SDA high, set clk_cnt=8, then drive SDA low and hold it stable; repeat with clk_cnt=3.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: for clk_cnt=8, filter samples occur at the interval floor(8/4)=2 enabled clocks, and busy rises only after the corresponding modeled filtered START latency. For clk_cnt=3, the zero-derived interval is treated as sampling on every enabled clock, and busy rises with the faster corresponding latency. In both cases the observed timing must track the configured clk_cnt-derived interval.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronized samples, filter_cnt reload/expiry, majority filtering, START detection, and registered busy; compare busy assertion cycles for both prescaler settings and verify the clk_cnt=8 latency is not replaced by an unrelated fixed interval.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, keep ena high with SCL high, bus idle, and clk_cnt=8. Start with SDA high, inject a raw SDA low pulse whose duration is insufficient for the synchronized samples and three-sample filter history to produce a filtered low majority, then return SDA high and remain idle.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because the raw transition does not persist long enough to produce the required filtered samples at floor(8/4)=2 enabled clocks, no filtered START is detected; busy remains low and does not rise from the glitch.
elements.check_method: Drive the pulse duration from the reference model's maximum non-majority-producing window, monitor filter_sample_event and start_condition, and assert that no filtered START event or busy assertion occurs while comparing the observed filter behavior against the clk_cnt-derived sampling schedule.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle with nReset high after reset release, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value that produces a timing tick, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 to model a released-high bus, then drive cmd=I2C_CMD_START (4'b0001) through an enabled timing tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0024: after the idle FSM accepts I2C_CMD_START, sda_oen becomes 0 during the START phase while scl_oen remains released (1), before SCL is driven low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use the in_idle and in_start_sequence probes to identify command acceptance and the START phase; compare sda_oen==0 and scl_oen==1 against the reference FSM model, and require that this SDA-low phase occurs only after the enabled acceptance tick.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle with nReset high after reset release, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value that produces a timing tick, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 to model a released-high bus, then drive cmd=I2C_CMD_NOP (4'b0000) through an enabled timing tick while the FSM is idle.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of REQ-0024: because cmd is not I2C_CMD_START, the START-specific condition does not occur; sda_oen does not fall to 0 while scl_oen remains released, the FSM stays idle, and no START sequence is entered.
elements.check_method: After the enabled timing tick and for the following observation window, sample sda_oen and scl_oen after each posedge and use in_idle/in_start_sequence probes; compare against the reference model and require sda_oen never equals 0 concurrently with scl_oen==1 and in_start_sequence==1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus externally released high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, wait until in_idle=1, then drive cmd=2 (I2C_CMD_STOP) through an enabled timing tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sda_oen first becomes 0 to drive SDA low; after SCL is released with scl_oen=1, sda_oen becomes 1 while SCL remains released high, producing the STOP sequence.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use the reference FSM model to compare the ordered sda_oen and scl_oen transitions; require the low-then-release sda_oen sequence and no alternate-command or idle-only behavior.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus externally released high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, wait until in_idle=1, then drive cmd=0 (NOP) through an enabled timing tick instead of cmd=2.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: sda_oen does not exhibit the STOP sequence; it remains in the idle released state and no STOP low-then-release transition occurs.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare sda_oen and scl_oen against the idle/NOP reference model and assert that no STOP-pattern transition is observed.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus released high, set clk_cnt=0, set din=0, and present cmd=0100 (I2C_CMD_WRITE) while in_idle is true. Hold the command through the enabled clock edge that accepts it, then provide filtered SCL high and low progression without arbitration interference.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0026: cmd=0100 is recognized as WRITE. sda_oen enters the WRITE data phase low, driving SDA low for din=0; scl_oen then releases SCL high during the WRITE stable-high phase and subsequently drives SCL low. The FSM returns idle and produces exactly one cmd_ack pulse, with no arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked assertion/reference-model comparison triggered by the command-acceptance clk_en tick. Check the ordered sda_oen low, scl_oen high, scl_oen low transitions, return to in_idle, one-cycle cmd_ack, and al remaining low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus released high, set clk_cnt=0, set din=1, and present cmd=0100 (I2C_CMD_WRITE) while in_idle is true. Hold the command through the enabled clock edge that accepts it, and keep external SDA high during the released SCL high phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0026: cmd=0100 is recognized as WRITE. sda_oen remains released high for the WRITE data phase because din=1; scl_oen releases SCL high for the stable-high phase and then drives SCL low. The FSM returns idle and produces exactly one cmd_ack pulse without asserting al.
elements.check_method: Compare sampled registered outputs against a WRITE reference model at every posedge. Assert the din=1 SDA release, SCL high-then-low phase ordering, one-cycle cmd_ack, and absence of arbitration loss.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus released high, set clk_cnt=0, and while in_idle is true present cmd=0011, an unsupported command encoding, for the same enabled acceptance interval used in the WRITE tests.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0026: cmd=0011 is not recognized as I2C_CMD_WRITE. sda_oen remains in idle/released behavior and does not enter a WRITE data phase; scl_oen does not perform the WRITE high-then-low timing sequence. The FSM remains idle and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Use assertions comparing the unsupported-command waveform with the WRITE reference waveform: no WRITE-phase sda_oen or scl_oen transitions, in_idle stays asserted, and cmd_ack has no pulse during the observation window.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, then deassert reset with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. While in_idle is observed, drive cmd through NOP=0000 and each unsupported encoding 0011, 0101, 0110, 0111, 1001, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, and 1111; hold each value through at least one enabled timing tick.
elements.expected_response: For the idle command and every unsupported command, the FSM remains in_idle, produces no command output sequence, and does not assert cmd_ack. This is the holding side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: At every enabled tick and for the following clock, sample in_idle and cmd_ack; assert in_idle remains high and cmd_ack remains low for all listed command encodings. Record a coverage bin for each encoding.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, then deassert reset with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Confirm in_idle is high, then drive cmd=I2C_CMD_READ=1000 and hold it through an enabled timing tick.
elements.expected_response: Unlike the idle or unsupported command case, the valid READ encoding is decoded while idle and the FSM leaves in_idle to execute the READ sequence, observable as in_read_sequence becoming high; cmd_ack occurs only at normal READ completion.
elements.check_method: Use a clock-synchronous assertion that, after the enabled acceptance tick, in_idle becomes low and in_read_sequence becomes high before command completion. Verify the observed port differs from the holding case by detecting the in_idle falling transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, present cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), drive din=0, hold the external SCL and SDA lines released high, and provide clk edges until the WRITE data-bit phase is reached and before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: This is the din=0 side of the requirement: during the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 0, driving SDA low; it remains consistent through the data establishment and released-SCL high phase, with no arbitration loss caused by the externally high SDA line.
elements.check_method: At every posedge while in_write_sequence and before cmd_ack, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference model; assert sda_oen==0 for din==0 and record coverage of the din=0 data-bit case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, present cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), drive din=1, hold the external SCL and SDA lines released high, and provide clk edges until the WRITE data-bit phase is reached and before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: This is the din=1 side of the requirement: during the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA high; the controller performs the normal released-high WRITE phase without arbitration loss when the external SDA line is high.
elements.check_method: At every posedge while in_write_sequence and before cmd_ack, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference model; assert sda_oen==1 for din==1 and record coverage of the din=1 data-bit case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, provide a released-high bus, set din=0, and issue cmd=WRITE=0100 while the FSM is idle. Hold din=0 until the WRITE command completes, and observe the SDA-setting phase after the command is accepted.
elements.expected_response: During the active WRITE SDA-setting phase, sda_oen is 0, so the DUT drives SDA low. This is the holding side of the requirement's shows condition: sda_oen is 0 when din is 0.
elements.check_method: At the first cycle with in_write_sequence asserted and during its SDA-setting phase, compare the registered sda_oen output against din using an assertion that requires sda_oen == 0 for din == 0; also verify the condition before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, provide a released-high bus, set din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE=0100 while the FSM is idle. Hold din=1 until the WRITE command completes, and observe the SDA-setting phase after the command is accepted.
elements.expected_response: During the active WRITE SDA-setting phase, sda_oen is 1, so the DUT releases SDA high. This is the contrasting side of the requirement's shows condition: sda_oen is 1 when din is 1; the opposite polarity would violate the requirement.
elements.check_method: At the first cycle with in_write_sequence asserted and during its SDA-setting phase, compare the registered sda_oen output against din using an assertion that requires sda_oen == 1 for din == 1; also verify the condition before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: With the module enabled and idle, issue a READ command, provide a valid filtered SCL-low phase, then release the external SCL line by driving scl_i low so the DUT has released SCL high and is in the READ sample window. Keep scl_i low for multiple enabled timing ticks.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in observed_via.shows: scl_oen remains 1 and its transition to 0 is postponed for as long as the externally supplied scl_i remains low; the READ sequence does not end the sample window or advance to the following phase.
elements.check_method: Use the READ-sequence and sample-window probes to identify the window, then monitor scl_oen after each posedge and compare against a reference model of the external open-drain SCL line and slave-clock-stretch wait behavior. Assert that scl_oen stays 1 throughout the low interval.

elements.stimulus: With the module enabled and idle, issue a READ command, provide a valid filtered SCL-low phase, then drive scl_i high after the DUT releases SCL and enters the READ sample window. Keep scl_i high through the required filtered SCL rising edge and subsequent timing progression.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise case in observed_via.shows: when the externally supplied SCL input is high, scl_oen transitions to 0 to end the READ sample window, after the applicable filtered/timing delay.
elements.check_method: Use the READ-sequence, read-sample-window, and filtered-SCL-rise probes; compare the observed registered scl_oen transition against a reference model including synchronizer, filter, and prescaler latency. Assert that scl_oen changes from 1 to 0 only after scl_i has been high long enough to produce filtered SCL high and the READ phase advances.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and the external bus initially high, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0. When the command releases SCL for its high phase, hold scl_i low long enough to pass synchronization and filtering, then drive scl_i high and allow the command to continue.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in observed_via.shows: cmd_ack does not pulse while scl_i remains low and the synchronized/filtered SCL is low; command completion is postponed. After scl_i is high long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL to become high, the command resumes and cmd_ack pulses once at normal completion.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer, filter sampling, and released-SCL wait. Assert that no cmd_ack pulse occurs during the filtered-low interval, then compare the post-release cmd_ack pulse and command phase timing with the model.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and the external bus initially high, issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0. During the released-SCL high phase, apply a scl_i low glitch shorter than the synchronizer/filter acceptance interval, then restore scl_i high before a filtered-low SCL value can be produced.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise case in observed_via.shows: the short raw scl_i glitch does not create a filtered clock-stretch condition, so cmd_ack progresses normally and pulses once when the command completes; completion is not postponed by the glitch.
elements.check_method: Compare synchronized samples, filter history/majority output, and cmd_ack timing against the reference model. Assert that the filtered SCL does not enter the stretch-low state and that the completion pulse occurs at the normal modeled cycle.

elements.stimulus: Hold the external I2C SDA line at 0, drive sda_i from that same external line, issue a READ command with ena high, allow the filtered SCL signal to rise after synchronization and filtering, and keep sda_i stable through the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the filtered SCL rising edge, dout captures 0, the filtered level corresponding to the externally supplied sda_i value.
elements.check_method: Use a bus model and reference filter model to identify the filtered SCL rising edge; sample dout after the corresponding posedge and compare it with the filtered sda_i value and the modeled external SDA line.

elements.stimulus: Hold the actual external I2C SDA line at 1, but substitute sda_i with a stable 0 rather than the pad or open-drain buffer value; issue a READ command with ena high and allow a filtered SCL rising edge to occur after synchronization and filtering.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: dout captures the filtered substituted sda_i level, 0, rather than the actual external SDA line level of 1; it therefore does not reflect the externally supplied line because sda_i was not connected to that line.
elements.check_method: Compare the external-bus model level, driven sda_i value, modeled filtered sda_i value, and dout after the filtered SCL rising edge; require dout to match filtered sda_i and differ from the actual external SDA level.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8. Present a released-high bus with filtered SCL high, then drive sda_i low and hold it long enough to pass the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample majority filter; issue START. After the START completes, drive filtered SDA low-to-high while filtered SCL remains high and hold it long enough to pass the same synchronization and filtering path.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the busy observation: busy rises only after the synchronized and filtered SDA high-to-low transition is recognized as START, and later falls only after the synchronized and filtered SDA low-to-high transition is recognized as STOP. No busy transition occurs before the corresponding filtered detection.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SDA synchronizer, filter sampling interval, three-sample majority value, and filtered edge detection. Compare busy after each settled posedge against the model at the filtered START and STOP events.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=8, filtered SCL high, and busy initially low, drive sda_i low for less than one filter sampling interval and release it high before the synchronized samples can produce a changed three-sample majority. Repeat with a short low-to-high pulse while filtered SDA remains low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the busy observation: busy does not rise for the short SDA pulse and does not fall for the short reverse pulse, because neither raw transition changes the synchronized and filtered SDA value. No START or STOP effect is observable at busy.
elements.check_method: Confirm with the synchronizer/filter reference model that the majority-filtered SDA remains unchanged, then assert that busy remains at its pre-stimulus value on every settled posedge.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and allow the FSM to reach the released-high WRITE arbitration-checking phase. Keep the external bus otherwise high but drive sda_i low long enough to pass synchronization and filtering while the controller expects SDA high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the al observation: al asserts when the synchronized and filtered SDA is low during the released-high WRITE arbitration-checking phase. The active WRITE aborts, cmd_ack is not pulsed for the aborted command, and both SDA and SCL output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the filtered SDA-low event while arbitration checking is active. Compare al, cmd_ack, and both output enables after each settled posedge, checking that al becomes one and remains asserted.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and wait for the released-high arbitration-checking phase. Apply an sda_i-low glitch shorter than one filter sampling interval, then restore sda_i high before the synchronized filter history can produce filtered SDA low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the al observation: al does not assert because the unfiltered short SDA glitch does not indicate arbitration loss to the filtered logic. The WRITE continues through its normal low phase and eventually produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Verify with the synchronizer/filter model that filtered SDA stays high throughout arbitration checking. Assert that al remains low and that the normal completion ack occurs without an abort.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, issue a READ command, and hold SCL released high for the READ sampling window. Drive sda_i to 0 and hold it long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to settle before the filtered SCL rising edge; repeat the transaction with sda_i held at 1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the dout observation: on each filtered SCL rising edge in the READ sampling window, dout captures the synchronized and filtered SDA value, yielding 0 in the first transaction and 1 in the second. The value is registered and remains stable until the next qualifying filtered SCL rise.
elements.check_method: Run the two-stage synchronizer, filter-majority, and filtered-SCL-edge reference model. At each modeled filtered SCL rising edge during READ, compare dout after the corresponding posedge with the modeled filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, issue a READ command, and hold filtered SCL high in the READ sampling window with filtered SDA initially high. Apply an sda_i-low pulse shorter than one filter sampling interval and arrange for it to end before the filtered SCL rising edge, so the synchronized three-sample majority remains high at that edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the dout observation: dout does not capture the unfiltered or arbitrarily timed low pulse; it captures and retains the filtered SDA value of 1 at the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to prove that filtered SDA remains high at the modeled filtered SCL rise, then compare registered dout after the posedge and ensure it is 1 rather than the transient raw sda_i value.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=START, and allow the START bit-level sequence to complete through its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: At the clock where the START command finishes, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle; it is low on the preceding and following clocks. This is the asserted side of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify START completion, then sample cmd_ack after each posedge and require the pattern 0, 1, 0 around the terminal completion clock.

elements.stimulus: Establish a busy transaction context as needed, set ena=1, issue cmd=STOP, provide a released bus, and allow the STOP sequence to complete through SDA release while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: At the clock where the STOP command finishes, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle; it is low before and after that cycle. This is the asserted side of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Track the STOP terminal phase with the timing reference model and compare the registered cmd_ack waveform for a single-cycle pulse aligned to command completion.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue cmd=READ, release SDA, provide a stable external SDA value, allow the read SCL-high sampling window and subsequent low phase to complete.
elements.expected_response: At the clock where the READ command finishes after its low phase, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle and is low on all other clocks. This is the asserted side of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to account for filtered SCL rising-edge sampling and identify READ completion; verify cmd_ack is a one-clock pulse at that completion.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0, keep SDA low-compatible and allow the write high phase and following low phase to complete without arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: At the clock where the WRITE command finishes, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle and is low before and after it. This is the asserted side of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Model the WRITE phase progression and completion, then compare cmd_ack after every posedge to require exactly one asserted cycle aligned with completion.

elements.stimulus: While idle and ena=1, issue cmd=NOP=0000 for multiple enabled timing ticks, then issue an unsupported command encoding such as 0011; do not start any valid command.
elements.expected_response: Because no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE command finishes, cmd_ack remains low on every clock. This is the otherwise side of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack against a reference model that has no active command and require it never asserts during the NOP and unsupported-command interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=START while the FSM is idle and the filtered bus is released high. Allow the START sequence to complete through its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: The START command completes and returns the command FSM to idle. cmd_ack is high on exactly the one clk cycle corresponding to command completion and is low on the immediately preceding and following clk cycles.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify START acceptance and its terminal completion edge; sample cmd_ack after each posedge and assert a single-cycle pulse exactly on that edge, with no adjacent-cycle assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP while the FSM is idle with bus inputs allowing the STOP sequence to proceed. Allow the sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, release SDA, and finish.
elements.expected_response: The STOP command completes and returns the command FSM to idle. cmd_ack is asserted high for exactly one clk cycle at the STOP completion edge and remains low before and after that cycle.
elements.check_method: Track the STOP terminal phase with a cycle-accurate reference model and compare the observed registered cmd_ack waveform against a one-cycle pulse aligned to the completion edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive din=0, and issue cmd=WRITE while the FSM is idle. Keep the external bus released except for the DUT's open-drain drive and allow the write bit to complete normally.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE command completes and returns the command FSM to idle without arbitration loss. cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle when the write terminal phase completes, with no pulse on any other cycle.
elements.check_method: Use the modeled prescaler and WRITE phase transitions to determine the completion edge, then assert that cmd_ack has one and only one high sample at that edge and is low on both neighboring cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ while the FSM is idle. Provide a normal released SCL waveform and stable external SDA data, allowing the read sample window, SCL-low phase, and command completion to occur.
elements.expected_response: The READ command completes and returns the command FSM to idle. cmd_ack is asserted high for exactly one clk cycle following the READ terminal phase and is low on every other cycle.
elements.check_method: Predict the READ completion edge from the filtered SCL/read-window model and compare the registered cmd_ack output cycle by cycle, requiring exactly one high cycle aligned with completion.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 while idle, then observe the command during its low phase and released-SCL high phase before the terminal phase is reached; do not allow the command to finish during the observation interval.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding side of the requirement: because the current WRITE command has not finished, cmd_ack must remain low throughout all non-terminal cycles. It must not pulse early; a one-cycle pulse is permitted only when the later terminal phase completes.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to mark every cycle before WRITE completion and assert cmd_ack=0 on those cycles; separately verify that the eventual completion produces exactly one pulse, distinguishing the required completion behavior from premature acknowledgment.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy low, hold scl_i high and sda_i high for enough enabled clocks to establish filtered idle levels.
