With ena high and cmd=N​​OP, drive sda_i low while continuing to hold scl_i high, and maintain the resulting bus levels through synchronization and majority-filter settling until start_condition is observed.
elements.expected_response: On the clock edge that processes the detected filtered START condition, busy rises to 1 and remains high until a STOP condition is detected. This is the 'busy rises after a START condition' side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-signal reference model to identify the start_condition processing edge, then sample busy after nonblocking updates on that posedge and assert busy==1; assert it does not remain low after START.

elements.stimulus: Establish busy high by holding scl_i high and driving a filtered START transition with sda_i from high to low, then hold the bus stable until busy is asserted. Next, while continuing to hold scl_i high, drive sda_i high and maintain the resulting bus levels through synchronization and majority-filter settling until stop_condition is observed.
elements.expected_response: On the clock edge that processes the detected filtered STOP condition, busy falls to 0 and remains low until a new START condition is detected. This is the 'busy falls after a STOP condition' side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-signal reference model to identify the stop_condition processing edge, then sample busy after nonblocking updates on that posedge and assert busy==0; assert it does not stay high after STOP.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so al is low. Issue START, then issue WRITE with din=1 and ena high. During the released-high WRITE arbitration-checking phase, hold the external SDA line low while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: This is the arbitration-loss condition described by the requirement; al asserts to indicate that arbitration was lost.
elements.check_method: Use the write_stable_high_phase and arbitration_checking probes to identify the checking interval, model the synchronizer/filter latency, and compare the sampled al output after the clock edge that processes filtered SDA low against an expected asserted value.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so al is low. Issue START, then issue a non-STOP command such as WRITE with din=0. While the command is active and filtered SCL is high, drive filtered SDA through a low-to-high transition to create an unexpected STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the unexpected-STOP arbitration-loss condition; al asserts to indicate that arbitration was lost.
elements.check_method: Use the active_command and stop_condition probes to qualify the transition as an unexpected STOP during an active command, then compare al after the registered status update with the reference model's asserted value.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so al is low. Issue START, then issue WRITE with din=1 and ena high. Keep external SDA released high throughout the released-high WRITE phase and do not generate a STOP condition during the active command.
elements.expected_response: Neither arbitration-loss condition occurs; al remains deasserted.
elements.check_method: Use the active_command, arbitration_checking, and write_stable_high_phase probes to verify the command reaches the relevant phases without an arbitration mismatch or unexpected STOP, and check that al stays low on every clock through command completion.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so al is low. Issue START, then issue WRITE with din=0 and ena high. During the released-high WRITE phase, keep SDA low as required by the open-drain write and do not generate an unexpected STOP.
elements.expected_response: A low SDA while writing din=0 is not an arbitration-loss condition; al remains deasserted.
elements.check_method: Use the in_write_sequence, arbitration_checking, and write_stable_high_phase probes to qualify the write, compare the filtered SDA level with din=0, and verify al remains low through completion.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and release it with ena=1. Issue a WRITE command with din=1, allow the command to reach its released-SDA arbitration-checking high phase, and externally drive SDA low while filtered SCL is high and filtered SDA is stably low.
elements.expected_response: The al output asserts on the clock processing the filtered low SDA during arbitration checking, the WRITE command aborts without cmd_ack, and both sda_oen and scl_oen are released.
elements.check_method: Use the arbitration_checking and write_stable_high_phase probes to identify the check window; compare al against a reference model using filtered SDA, and verify no cmd_ack occurs before the FSM returns to in_idle.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and release it with ena=1. Issue a WRITE command with din=1, allow the command to reach its released-SDA arbitration-checking high phase, and keep the externally resolved and filtered SDA line high.
elements.expected_response: The al output does not assert in response to this arbitration-checking phase; the WRITE proceeds through SCL release and pull-down, then completes with a one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the arbitration_checking and write_stable_high_phase probes and a filtered-line reference model; assert al remains 0 through completion and check that cmd_ack is generated exactly once.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and release it with ena=1. Issue a READ command and, while active_command is asserted, drive filtered SDA from high to low and hold filtered SCL high long enough to create a filtered STOP condition that was not requested by the controller.
elements.expected_response: The stop_condition event causes al to assert, the active READ command aborts, and no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Use active_command and stop_condition probes to qualify the event; compare al and cmd_ack with a reference FSM model and verify the FSM returns to in_idle with both output enables released.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and release it with ena=1. Issue a STOP command and provide a released-high bus so the controller executes the requested STOP sequence, including SDA low, SCL release, and SDA release while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: The al output does not assert for the STOP condition because STOP was the requested command; the STOP sequence completes and produces one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use in_stop_sequence and stop_condition probes to distinguish the requested STOP from an unexpected active-command STOP; check al remains 0 and compare the output-enable sequence and single cmd_ack against the reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a READ command on an enabled timing tick. Allow the controller to release SDA and SCL for the read window. Hold the external SDA line low, keep SCL low initially, then drive SCL high and maintain both lines long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a filtered SCL rising edge while filtered SDA is 0.
elements.expected_response: At the posedge that processes the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 0, which is the filtered SDA value for that edge.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of synchronization, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered-edge detection. At the modeled filtered SCL rising edge, compare the post-posedge registered dout value with the modeled filtered SDA value and require dout=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a READ command on an enabled timing tick. Allow the controller to release SDA and SCL for the read window. Hold the external SDA line high, keep SCL low initially, then drive SCL high and maintain both lines long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a filtered SCL rising edge while filtered SDA is 1.
elements.expected_response: At the posedge that processes the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 1, which is the filtered SDA value for that edge.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of synchronization, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered-edge detection. At the modeled filtered SCL rising edge, compare the post-posedge registered dout value with the modeled filtered SDA value and require dout=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a READ command on an enabled timing tick. Allow the controller to release SDA, but hold the externally driven SCL low so no filtered SCL rising edge occurs. Change the external SDA level and keep the read window active for multiple enabled clocks without allowing filtered SCL to rise.
elements.expected_response: dout does not update to the changed filtered SDA value because no filtered SCL rising edge occurred; it retains its previously registered value until a filtered SCL rising edge is processed.
elements.check_method: The reference model shall confirm that no filtered_scl_rise event occurs during the observation window. Sample dout after every posedge and require it to remain unchanged despite the SDA change.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, then apply rst high for a clock and release it. Keep ena low and then high while the FSM remains idle; sample scl_o and scl_oen after each reset and clock edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o is 0 at every observation, including asynchronous reset, synchronous reset, idle, and ena transitions, independently of scl_oen. The contrasting side would be scl_o becoming 1 or otherwise not remaining constantly low; that is a failure.
elements.check_method: At each reset and clock-edge sample, compare scl_o exactly against 1'b0 and assert that no sample differs. Independently record scl_oen to ensure scl_o is not being used as the SCL line-control output.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, clk_cnt=0, and the external SCL/SDA bus released high, issue valid START, WRITE with din=0, READ, and STOP commands sequentially, allowing each command to complete before issuing the next. Observe every clock edge while scl_oen changes between driven-low and released-high phases.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows under contrasting SCL control phases: scl_o remains 0 throughout START, WRITE, READ, STOP, and idle, including every interval where scl_oen is 0 or 1. The contrasting side would be scl_o=1 at any observation or scl_o changing with scl_oen; either result fails the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use a reference trace to identify all scl_oen transitions and command phases, then assert scl_o == 1'b0 on every sampled clock edge before, during, and after each transition. Flag any scl_o value other than zero, especially one correlated with scl_oen.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high, issue cmd=I2C_CMD_START, and advance clocks using the reference timing model until the START sequence reaches its SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: During the active command's SCL-low phase, scl_oen is 0; because the control is active-low open-drain, the modeled SCL bus line is driven low. This is the holding case in which scl_oen=0 indicates that SCL is driven low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen with the reference FSM phase and assert scl_oen==0 in the SCL-low phase; independently resolve the open-drain bus model and assert SCL is low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high, issue cmd=I2C_CMD_START, and observe the START sequence before or after its SCL-low phase whenever the reference timing model indicates that SCL is released.
elements.expected_response: While the command phase releases SCL, scl_oen is 1 and the modeled SCL bus line remains high when no external participant drives it low. This is the contrasting case in which the requirement's behavior does not hold: scl_oen=1 indicates that SCL is released rather than driven low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen with the reference FSM phase and assert scl_oen==1 in every SCL-released phase; resolve the open-drain bus model and confirm the line is high with the external bus released.

elements.stimulus: Hold ena high, provide a released-high bus, and issue the START command. Advance the command using the enabled timing ticks until the START sequence reaches a phase in which the controller releases SCL.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed port behavior: scl_oen is 1, releasing SCL so the external pull-up can drive it high; sda_o remains 0 at every observation.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare scl_oen and sda_o against a reference START-sequence phase model; bin the release phase and assert scl_oen == 1 and sda_o == 1'b0.

elements.stimulus: Hold ena high, provide a released-high bus, and issue the START command. Advance through the release phase until the START sequence reaches its subsequent phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the observed port behavior: scl_oen is 0, driving SCL low; sda_o remains 0, confirming the constant-low SDA drive value.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare scl_oen and sda_o against the reference START-sequence phase model; bin the SCL-drive-low phase and assert scl_oen == 1'b0 and sda_o == 1'b0.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release both resets, then run the DUT through idle and complete START, WRITE with din=0, WRITE with din=1, READ, and STOP sequences with ena high and a normally released bus.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sda_o is continuously 1'b0 at every sampled clock, including reset, idle, and every command phase; SDA line behavior is not represented by a nonzero sda_o value.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after reset values settle, assert sda_o == 1'b0 for the entire test and record a coverage bin for each idle and command phase.

elements.stimulus: Issue START, then WRITE commands with din=0 and din=1, and then STOP; provide the required filtered SCL timing and allow each command to reach its SDA ownership phases.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting ownership-control case: sda_o remains 1'b0 while sda_oen changes between 0 when the master drives SDA low and 1 when it releases SDA; the observed SDA ownership transitions therefore occur through sda_oen, not through sda_o.
elements.check_method: Trace sda_o and sda_oen across each command phase. Assert sda_o == 0 on every sample, and compare each expected drive/release transition against sda_oen (0 for drive, 1 for release), with bins for both enable values and both din values.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1 and issue a supported START command (cmd=0001) while scl_i and sda_i are high; continue clocking until the accepted START sequence reaches its SDA-driving phase.
elements.expected_response: During the START SDA-driving phase, sda_oen becomes 0 after the corresponding registered update, indicating the active-low open-drain SDA enable is asserted and SDA is driven low; when the phase ends, sda_oen returns to 1.
elements.check_method: Use the command-sequence reference model and sample sda_oen after each posedge. Match the in_start_sequence probe and verify sda_oen=0 throughout the SDA-driving phase, followed by sda_oen=1 after release.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1 and issue a supported START command (cmd=0001) while scl_i and sda_i are high; clock through the initial START phase in which the controller releases SDA before it asserts the SDA-driving phase.
elements.expected_response: In the initial SDA-released phase, sda_oen remains 1, indicating the contrasting side of the observation: SDA is released rather than driven low. It must change to 0 only when the subsequent SDA-driving phase is reached.
elements.check_method: Use the in_start_sequence probe and compare the registered sda_oen value after each posedge against the phase reference model: require sda_oen=1 before SDA driving and require the later transition to sda_oen=0.

elements.stimulus: With the DUT operating, drive nReset low asynchronously between clk rising edges and hold it low; use a released external SDA bus with sda_i high, then sample sda_oen after reset takes effect.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed behavior: sda_oen becomes 1 and remains high, releasing SDA so the external pull-up drives the SDA line high; sda_o remains 0.
elements.check_method: At the asynchronous reset event and while nReset remains low, compare sda_oen to 1 and verify the resolved open-drain SDA line is high when no external device drives it low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, deassert nReset, set ena high, provide a released-high bus, issue the START command encoding cmd=0001, and advance clocks until the START sequence reaches its phase that pulls SDA low while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting side of the observed behavior: sda_oen is 0, driving SDA low rather than releasing it; with sda_o=0 and no external override, the resolved SDA line is low.
elements.check_method: Use the in_start_sequence probe and sample registered sda_oen after each posedge; identify the SDA-low START phase and assert sda_oen=0 and resolved SDA=0 there, contrasting it with the reset release case.

elements.stimulus: Review the specification text under the "Implementation details" heading and confirm that this numbered-list introduction supplies no command, input, reset, timing, state-transition, or output condition.
elements.expected_response: No DUT output behavior, state transition, timing constraint, or interface response is required or asserted for this requirement.
elements.check_method: Manual specification-audit check: verify the requirement trace contains no executable behavioral expectation and that no additional DUT-directed test is generated from this scaffolding text.

elements.stimulus: After reset, leave cmd=N​​OP and ena high while observing the module in idle; also vary scl_i and sda_i between high and low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_o remains 0 and sda_o remains 0 for every sampled interface observation, regardless of external SCL/SDA levels. Neither output directly drives its bus line high.
elements.check_method: At every clocking-block observation after reset settles, assert scl_o===1'b0 and sda_o===1'b0; flag any high value as a failure.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and a released-high external bus, issue START, WRITE with din=0, WRITE with din=1, READ, and STOP commands, allowing each command to progress through its active sequence and completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting-case check: even during all command phases that manipulate SCL or SDA, scl_o and sda_o remain 0. If either output becomes 1, that is the noncompliant 'otherwise' side of the observed behavior and indicates the module directly drives that line high.
elements.check_method: Continuously sample scl_o and sda_o throughout every active command sequence and assert both are always zero, including at each output-enable transition and command acknowledgement.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset asynchronously, deassert it, then exercise idle and valid START, STOP, WRITE, and READ commands with ena high while varying din and the external SCL/SDA line responses. Include synchronous rst during idle and during an active command.
elements.expected_response: The holding side of REQ-0048 is observed: scl_o and sda_o remain constant at 1'b0 at every sampled clock edge, during asynchronous and synchronous reset, and throughout every command phase and idle state.
elements.check_method: At every clocking-block sample, assert scl_o === 1'b0 and sda_o === 1'b0; include asynchronous samples while nReset is asserted and retain a coverage bin for reset, idle, START, STOP, WRITE, READ, and arbitration-related phases.

elements.stimulus: Run the module through reset, idle, and an active command while injecting a fault that forces or mutates either scl_o or sda_o to 1'b1 for at least one sampled clock edge, then remove the fault and continue operation.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting, non-holding side of REQ-0048 is detected: any sampled scl_o or sda_o value other than 1'b0 is reported as a requirement failure; the uncorrupted DUT must never produce this non-constant behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a fault-injection or mutation test to force each output high independently and together, and verify the checker raises an assertion failure on the first violating sample. Confirm the baseline run has no such failure.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue a START command and observe the clocked output-enable values during the START sequence, including the phase where SCL is driven low.
elements.expected_response: During the SCL pull-low phase, scl_oen is 0 and the open-drain bus model observes SCL low. This is the asserted-low side of the requirement's shows statement: scl_oen is 0 when SCL is pulled low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen to the expected START phase and resolve SCL as low when scl_oen=0; record bins for asserted-low enable and observed-low line.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue a START command and observe the clocked output-enable values during the START sequence, including the phase where SCL is released high.
elements.expected_response: During the SCL release phase, scl_oen is 1 and, with no external low driver, the open-drain bus model observes SCL high/released. This is the released-high side of the requirement's shows statement: scl_oen is 1 when SCL is released.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen to the expected START phase and resolve SCL as high when scl_oen=1 and the external driver is released; record bins for released-high enable and observed-released line.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue a WRITE command with din=0 and observe the clocked output-enable values through the data-drive phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase for din=0, sda_oen is 0 and the open-drain bus model observes SDA low. This is the asserted-low side of the requirement's shows statement: sda_oen is 0 when SDA is pulled low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare sda_oen to din=0 phase expectations and resolve SDA as low when sda_oen=0; record bins for asserted-low enable and observed-low line.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue a WRITE command with din=1 and observe the clocked output-enable values through the data-drive and released-high phases.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase for din=1, sda_oen is 1 and, with no external low driver, the open-drain bus model observes SDA high/released. This is the released-high side of the requirement's shows statement: sda_oen is 1 when SDA is released.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare sda_oen to din=1 phase expectations and resolve SDA as high when sda_oen=1 and the external driver is released; record bins for released-high enable and observed-released line.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a valid START command while scl_i and sda_i are externally released high. Advance the command using the configured clk_cnt until the START sequence reaches its interval with SCL released.
elements.expected_response: During the stable released-SCL interval, scl_oen is 1, identifying the holding side of REQ-0050: SCL is not actively driven low and the external pull-up provides the high logic level on the bus, observed as scl_i high when no external participant drives it low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge while the START sequence is in the released-SCL interval, compare scl_oen against the reference FSM and sample scl_i after bus resolution; require scl_oen=1 and scl_i=1 for the no-external-low case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a valid START command with the bus externally released high. Advance the command using clk_cnt through the START sequence until the controller enters its SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: During the stable SCL-low interval, scl_oen is 0, identifying the contrasting side of REQ-0050: the controller actively pulls SCL low rather than obtaining the high level from the external pull-up, and the resolved scl_i is low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the START SCL-low phase, compare scl_oen with the reference FSM and sample the resolved scl_i; require scl_oen=0 and scl_i=0.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=5, ena=1, rst=0, and nReset=0 asynchronously between clock edges; keep nReset low across at least one posedge, then deassert nReset.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: while reset is active, cnt is loaded from clk_cnt and clk_en_tick is asserted on each applicable clock; after reset release, timing starts from the loaded value.
elements.check_method: At the asynchronous reset assertion and following posedge, compare clk_en_tick against the reference divider model and verify the modeled counter reload to 5. Sample after nonblocking assignments settle.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=5, nReset=1, ena=1, and assert rst=1 before a rising edge; hold rst high for one or more posedges, then deassert rst.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: on every posedge while synchronous reset is active, cnt is loaded from clk_cnt and clk_en_tick is asserted; after rst deassertion, timing starts from the loaded value.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model synchronized to posedge clk; compare clk_en_tick on reset cycles and verify the modeled counter value is reloaded to 5 rather than decremented.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=3, release both resets, keep ena=1, and avoid clock stretching or synchronization events. Starting immediately after reset release, run enough posedges for the reference counter to decrement from its reload value to zero.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: on the clock where cnt reaches zero, cnt reloads to 3 and clk_en_tick is asserted; the divider then begins another decrement interval.
elements.check_method: Drive a cycle-accurate reference counter initialized to 3, predict the zero-expiry cycle and reload, and compare the predicted tick sequence with clk_en_tick after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=7, release both resets, and hold ena=0 for several rising edges, then set ena=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: while ena is low, cnt is loaded from 7 and clk_en_tick is asserted rather than the counter decrementing. When ena becomes high, normal countdown behavior resumes from the reloaded value.
elements.check_method: Compare each disabled-cycle clk_en_tick to 1 and verify the reference counter is reloaded to 7 on every disabled cycle; after enabling, compare subsequent ticks with the normal divider model.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=4, release reset, issue a valid START command with ena=1, and when the command sequence has released SCL high, externally pull scl_i low while the DUT has released SCL; hold the external low long enough to create a filtered SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: when multi-master clock synchronization occurs, cnt reloads to 4 and clk_en_tick is asserted; timing restarts from the reload value rather than continuing the prior countdown.
elements.check_method: Use the filter/synchronizer reference model to identify the scl_sync_event cycle, then verify clk_en_tick is asserted on that event and the reference divider state is reloaded to 4.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=4, release both resets, keep ena=1, do not issue a command, do not induce SCL synchronization, and sample during a cycle in which the reference cnt is nonzero after a prior reload.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting, non-holding side of the requirement: when reset is inactive, ena is high, no synchronization occurs, and cnt is nonzero, cnt decrements by one and clk_en_tick remains deasserted.
elements.check_method: Drive the reference counter through a reload followed by a nonzero-count cycle; compare clk_en_tick to 0 and verify the modeled counter decrements rather than reloads.

elements.stimulus: Set nReset=0 and then release it; set rst=0, ena=1, and a nonzero clk_cnt. Issue a valid START, STOP, WRITE, or READ command on an enabled timing tick. When the active command reaches its released-SCL phase, drive the external bus SCL low and hold scl_i=0 long enough for filtered SCL to remain low and slave_wait to assert. Keep ena=1 and hold scl_i=0 for multiple expected prescaler periods.
elements.expected_response: This is the slave-wait side of the requirement's shows distinction: while scl_oen=1 and the externally held SCL remains low, slave_wait remains asserted, the internal counter holds its value, and clk_en_tick remains deasserted on every enabled clock. The active command does not advance and cmd_ack does not pulse during the hold.
elements.check_method: Use the slave_wait and clk_en_tick probes sampled after each posedge. Assert slave_wait=1 throughout the hold and assert that no clk_en_tick event occurs or command-phase transition is observed during the hold; also verify cmd_ack remains low.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, ena, clk_cnt, and valid-command sequence, but after the command reaches its released-SCL phase drive scl_i=1 and maintain it long enough for filtered SCL to become high. If first exercising the stretch, release scl_i=1 only after observing the hold in TP-0000.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-slave-wait side of the requirement's shows distinction: once filtered SCL is released high, slave_wait deasserts, the counter is allowed to progress, clk_en_tick asserts according to clk_cnt, and the command advances toward its normal completion; cmd_ack may subsequently pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the slave_wait and clk_en_tick probes plus command-state/output observations. After filtered SCL becomes high, require slave_wait=0 and observe a clk_en_tick event within the modeled prescaler schedule, followed by the expected next phase and eventual command completion when no other wait condition exists.

elements.stimulus: No stimulus; document and execute no behavioral check for this scaffolding item.
elements.expected_response: No output behavior is required or expected by REQ-0053.
elements.check_method: Review the traceability report to confirm REQ-0053@1 is covered only by this vacuity element and that no DUT output comparison is claimed.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted and ena=1, issue a supported WRITE command with din=1, advance the controller until scl_oen=1 during the command's SCL-high phase, and hold the external scl_i line low long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL value to remain low.
elements.expected_response: The master has released SCL while filtered SCL remains low, so slave_wait is asserted; the WRITE timing phase remains held pending SCL release. This is the asserting side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor scl_oen, the filtered-SCL/reference-model value, slave_wait, clk_en_tick, and in_write_sequence. Compare slave_wait against the reference model and verify it is 1 whenever scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL=0 during this phase.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted and ena=1, issue a supported WRITE command with din=1, advance until scl_oen=1 during the command's SCL-high phase, initially hold scl_i low, then release the external SCL line high and keep it high until synchronization and the three-sample filter produce filtered SCL=1.
elements.expected_response: Once filtered SCL is high, the condition for slave clock stretching is absent, so slave_wait is deasserted and the controller may resume its timed WRITE progression. This is the non-asserting side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare slave_wait with a reference model of synchronized and filtered SCL while scl_oen=1. Verify slave_wait transitions from 1 to 0 only after filtered SCL becomes 1, and that subsequent clk_en_tick/FSM progress is not blocked by slave_wait.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena=1 and an idle released-high bus, issue a supported START command (cmd=4'b0001). When the command reaches its SCL-release phase, externally hold SCL low long enough for the synchronized and majority-filtered SCL value to remain low.
elements.expected_response: While scl_oen is 1 and filtered SCL remains low, slave_wait asserts, indicating that the external slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low. The controller remains in the SCL-release wait condition for as long as the filtered SCL remains low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use the filter/synchronizer reference model to identify the interval with scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL=0; require slave_wait=1 throughout that interval and require no command-phase advancement before filtered SCL becomes high.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena=1 and an idle released-high bus, issue the same supported START command (cmd=4'b0001). When the command reaches its SCL-release phase, do not externally pull SCL low; keep the bus released so synchronized and filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case: scl_oen is 1 but filtered SCL is high, so slave_wait remains 0 and the controller proceeds beyond the SCL-release phase on subsequent enabled timing ticks; the external participant is not indicated as holding SCL low.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the interval with scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL=1; require slave_wait=0 and verify that the FSM advances on the next modeled clk_en tick rather than remaining in the wait condition.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0, and keep scl_i high until the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1). Then hold scl_i low so filtered SCL remains low and slave_wait remains active; after several enabled clock cycles, release scl_i high and keep it high until the command can complete.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding-case side of the cmd_ack difference: cmd_ack must not pulse while SCL remains held low and slave_wait is active, demonstrating that the timing counter and command progression are paused. After scl_i is released and filtered SCL becomes high, timing resumes and cmd_ack eventually pulses exactly once for the WRITE command.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for divider expiration, filtered SCL, slave_wait, and command phases. Assert no cmd_ack during every cycle with slave_wait=1, then assert one cmd_ack after slave_wait clears and no duplicate pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0, and keep scl_i high throughout the released-SCL high phase so slave_wait never becomes active.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise side of the cmd_ack difference: because SCL is not held low, the timing counter continues and the command progresses normally; cmd_ack eventually pulses exactly once without waiting for a slave-wait interval.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to predict command completion with no slave-wait pause. Check that slave_wait remains inactive, cmd_ack is absent before the modeled completion point, and a single one-clock cmd_ack pulse occurs at completion.

elements.stimulus: Apply no requirement-specific stimulus; record an idle trace without interpreting any DUT behavior as required by REQ-0057.
elements.expected_response: No specific output, state transition, timing, or protocol behavior is required by REQ-0057.
elements.check_method: Review the test result and coverage database to confirm this item imposes no behavioral comparison and is covered only by documenting the absence of a stated obligation.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue a valid START command on a released-high bus. After the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1) during the command sequence, drive the external SCL line low and hold it long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a falling edge on filtered SCL.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of the required observation: while scl_oen=1, the detected falling edge of filtered SCL asserts the scl_sync synchronization event, observable on the scl_sync_event probe.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronization, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered-edge detection. While scl_oen=1, compare the predicted filtered-SCL falling-edge cycle with the scl_sync_event probe and require exactly one asserted event for that edge.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue a valid START command. During a period in which the controller has released SCL (scl_oen=1), keep the external SCL line high; additionally apply a low pulse shorter than the filter's majority qualification interval and return SCL high before filtered SCL falls.
elements.expected_response: Negative side of the required observation: because no falling edge occurs on filtered SCL while SCL is released, the controller does not assert the scl_sync synchronization event; scl_sync_event remains deasserted for the entire filtered-out pulse.
elements.check_method: Run the synchronized/filter reference model to confirm that filtered SCL remains high and has no falling edge, then assert that scl_sync_event is never asserted during the released-SCL interval.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt. Issue a START command and allow it to complete, then issue a WRITE command with din=0. During the WRITE released-SCL-high phase, when scl_oen=1 and the filtered SCL is high, externally pull scl_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered SCL falling edge; then release scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement: scl_oen remains 1 while the shared SCL is externally held low, the next commanded SCL control transition is postponed, and the WRITE does not advance through the high phase until filtered SCL returns high. After release, the command resumes and completes normally.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronizer, filter, scl_sync_event, divider reload, and FSM timing. At each posedge compare scl_oen against the model, verify scl_oen stays 1 throughout the filtered-SCL-low interval, verify no expected high-phase-to-low-phase transition occurs during that interval, and verify progression resumes only after filtered SCL is high.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same sequence with ena=1, the same nonzero clk_cnt, START completion, and WRITE din=0, but keep scl_i released high throughout the WRITE released-SCL-high phase so no external filtered SCL falling edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting no-force case of the requirement: scl_oen advances from the released-high phase to the next commanded SCL phase at the normal timing boundary, without the postponement caused by another bus participant holding SCL low.
elements.check_method: Run the same reference model and compare the observed scl_oen transition cycle with the no-stretch timing prediction. Confirm that no scl_sync_event occurs, scl_oen does not remain high beyond the normal boundary, and the WRITE completes without an externally forced SCL-low delay.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to a nonzero value such as 8, establish a released-high bus, issue START and wait for its command completion, then issue WRITE with din=0. When the WRITE operation reaches its released SCL-high phase with scl_oen=1, have another bus master pull scl_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered SCL falling edge while the DUT still has scl_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: The synchronized SCL falling edge is detected while scl_oen remains 1. The DUT reloads its timing counter and restarts low-period timing; scl_oen remains 1 during the restarted timing interval and transitions to 0 only after the resynchronized low-period timing completes. The WRITE then continues without an unintended synchronization-shortened phase.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the synchronizers, filter, counter reload, and low-period timing. At each settled posedge compare the model's filtered SCL falling-edge event and expected scl_oen transition against the DUT waveform, confirming that scl_oen stays high through the restarted interval and changes low only at the resynchronized boundary.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, ena=1, clk_cnt=8, released-high bus, START completion, and WRITE din=0 sequence, but do not inject any external SCL falling edge during the WRITE released-high phase; keep scl_i high until the DUT reaches the normal WRITE low-phase boundary.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting no-synchronization case: without an external filtered SCL falling edge while scl_oen is 1, scl_oen transitions to 0 at the normal WRITE low-phase boundary without the synchronization-induced delay or counter restart.
elements.check_method: Use the same cycle-accurate reference model with no scl_sync_event and compare the DUT scl_oen waveform. Confirm that the low transition occurs at the ordinary WRITE boundary and that its timing differs from TP-0000 by the absence of the synchronization reload interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value. Issue a READ command while scl_i and sda_i are stable low, then allow the READ sequence to release SCL and drive sda_i high. Hold scl_i high and sda_i high long enough for both inputs to pass the two-stage synchronization and filter sampling path, producing a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: dout captures the synchronized and filtered SDA value of 1 at the qualifying filtered SCL rising edge and shows the new value after the registered output update; the raw input transition does not affect dout before the synchronization and filtering latency has elapsed.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the two-stage cSCL/cSDA synchronizers, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered SCL edge detection. At each posedge, compare dout with the model only after nonblocking updates settle, and verify the capture occurs on the modeled filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish a READ operation with dout known to 0 and keep the filtered SCL low. While the READ sequence is active, toggle sda_i from 0 to 1 for less than the combined two-stage synchronization and filter qualification latency, then return sda_i to 0 before a qualifying filtered SCL rising edge occurs. Do not hold the transition long enough to change the filtered SDA value.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: dout retains its previous value of 0; the short raw sda_i transition does not immediately change dout and produces no qualifying filtered SCL rising-edge sample. Any later dout update may occur only at a subsequent qualifying filtered SCL rising edge after synchronized and filtered inputs have settled.
elements.check_method: Run the same cycle-accurate synchronization and filtering reference model, inject the short raw transition at a modeled sampling boundary, and assert that dout remains 0 on every posedge before the next modeled filtered SCL rising edge. Check that no dout change is attributed directly to the raw transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy low, set ena=1, clk_cnt=8, hold scl_i high and sda_i high for baseline, then drive sda_i low for at least 8 enabled clk cycles while keeping scl_i high. Align observation to posedges and continue until the synchronized samples have been admitted through multiple filter-counter sampling opportunities.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in REQ-0062's `shows`: busy remains unchanged immediately after the raw SDA transition, then changes to 1 only after the filter counter reaches its sampling opportunity, synchronized SDA samples are shifted into the fSDA history, and the resulting filtered START condition is detected.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage SDA synchronizer, filter-counter reload/cadence, three-sample history updates, and filtered START detection. Assert that filter_sample_event occurs at the modeled cadence and that busy changes only on or after the modeled filtered START event, not at the raw transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy low, set ena=1, clk_cnt=8, hold scl_i high and sda_i high. Drive sda_i low for one enabled clk cycle positioned between filter-counter sampling opportunities, then return sda_i high before the next opportunity; keep scl_i high and allow enough cycles for the synchronizer and filter to process the transient.
elements.expected_response: This is the `otherwise` case in REQ-0062's `shows`: busy remains unchanged throughout because the transient is not admitted into the fSDA filter history and therefore does not produce a filtered START condition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that no filter sample captures the low transient into the three-sample history and that no filtered START event occurs. Assert that busy remains 0 and does not respond directly to the raw SDA transition.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release nReset with rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i and sda_i high long enough for the synchronized histories to become all ones, then drive sda_i low stably for enough enabled filter samples to shift three low SDA samples while keeping scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the filter updates produce an SDA history with a low majority while the SCL history remains majority high, busy rises on the registered observation corresponding to the filtered START condition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter-sample events, three-sample histories, and 2-of-3 majority values; compare the modeled SDA-majority transition with the registered busy output and require a busy rising event only at that transition.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release nReset with rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i and sda_i high until the histories are all high, then inject an SDA-low pulse aligned so the synchronized/filter model shifts exactly one low sample into the SDA history before returning sda_i high; keep scl_i high throughout.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because the SDA history never has a low majority while the SCL history is majority high, busy does not rise and no filtered START indication is observed.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that the SDA history contains at most one low sample at every filter update and that its majority remains high; assert that busy stays low for the complete injection and recovery window.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous nReset low, release it, and allow the filter histories and busy status to initialize high and low respectively. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, hold scl_i high, and keep sda_i high except for one synchronized/filter sampling interval in which sda_i is driven low before returning high; do not issue a command.
elements.expected_response: The short SDA glitch is the non-holding side of the observed behavior: three-sample majority filtering rejects it, filtered SDA does not produce a high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high, and busy remains low without pulsing or transitioning.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage SDA synchronizer, filter sampling interval, three-sample history, and majority value. At every settled posedge after the glitch, compare the modeled filtered START condition and the registered busy output; assert that busy remains 0 throughout.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous nReset low, release it, and allow the filter histories and busy status to initialize high and low respectively. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, hold scl_i high and sda_i high, then drive sda_i low continuously for at least two valid synchronized filter samples and keep it low long enough for the three-sample majority output to change.
elements.expected_response: The persistent SDA transition is the holding-side contrast: filtered SDA changes from high to low while filtered SCL is high, a filtered START condition is detected, and busy rises to 1 after the registered detection update.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to predict synchronizer, sampling, three-sample majority, and filtered START timing. Compare the predicted filtered SDA transition and START event with the DUT behavior, and verify that busy asserts on the following registered update and remains asserted.

elements.stimulus: Do not apply a requirement-specific stimulus; record the item as inactive scaffolding during testplan review.
elements.expected_response: No DUT output, state transition, timing, or protocol behavior is required by this item.
elements.check_method: Review the generated testplan and checker configuration to confirm that no DUT assertion or behavioral comparison is derived from REQ-0065; mark the coverage bin complete when the item is explicitly classified as non-constraining.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus released high, establish filtered SDA=1 and filtered SCL=1. Then drive sda_i low while keeping scl_i high long enough for synchronization and the majority filter to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition; keep the inputs stable through the detection sample.
elements.expected_response: START side of the condition: the start_condition probe asserts when filtered SDA falls while filtered SCL is high.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample majority value, and delayed filtered SDA. At the modeled filtered SDA falling edge with filtered SCL=1, compare the start_condition probe against an expected one-cycle assertion.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, establish filtered SDA=1 and filtered SCL=0. Drive sda_i low while keeping scl_i low long enough for the filtered SDA high-to-low transition, then keep both inputs stable; do not allow filtered SCL to become high during the SDA transition.
elements.expected_response: Non-START side of the condition: start_condition remains deasserted because the filtered SDA fall did not occur while filtered SCL was high.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to identify the filtered SDA falling edge and verify filtered SCL=0 at that edge. Compare the start_condition probe to an expected deasserted value and ensure no assertion occurs for the transition.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive scl_i=1 continuously. First hold sda_i=0 long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to establish filtered SDA low; then drive sda_i=1 and hold it high through the synchronization and filter sampling latency.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered SDA transition from low to high is processed while filtered SCL is high, the controller asserts stop_condition. This is the requirement-holds side of the STOP detection behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the stop_condition probe and a reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, three-sample majority filter, and delayed filtered SDA value. Compare the probe at each enabled clock and require assertion only at the modeled filtered low-to-high transition with filtered SCL high.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. First hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 long enough for filtered SDA low, then drive scl_i=0 and hold it low until filtered SCL is low; while filtered SCL remains low, drive sda_i=1 and hold it long enough for filtered SDA to rise.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA low-to-high transition occurring while filtered SCL is low does not assert stop_condition. This is the requirement-does-not-hold contrast side.
elements.check_method: Use the stop_condition probe and the same synchronizer/filter reference model to identify the filtered SDA rising edge and verify that stop_condition remains deasserted because the modeled filtered SCL is low.

elements.stimulus: Apply no DUT stimulus attributable to the numbered-list marker "7.".
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, output, state transition, or timing response is required by this requirement.
elements.check_method: Requirements-review check confirming that the marker introduces no behavioral assertion and that no additional DUT check is generated from it.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and establish filtered SCL high with filtered SDA high. Drive SDA high-to-low while SCL remains high long enough for the synchronizer and three-sample filter to produce start_condition=1, then hold the bus without generating a STOP condition for multiple enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: This is the 'busy is high after the detected START condition and remains high until the detected STOP condition' side of the requirement: busy is low before the filtered START, becomes high after the registered START detection, and remains high for the entire interval while no filtered STOP is detected.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization, filtering, and start_condition detection. Sample busy after each posedge after nonblocking updates settle; compare the registered busy value against the model and assert that it has no low cycle between the detected START and a subsequently generated STOP.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and establish filtered SCL high with filtered SDA high; verify the bus remains in the no-START condition, then generate a filtered START followed by a filtered STOP by driving SDA low and later high while SCL remains high, holding each level long enough to pass the filter.
elements.expected_response: This is the 'busy is low before the START condition is detected and after the STOP condition is detected' side of the requirement: busy remains low before START, becomes high after START detection, and returns low after STOP detection.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered START and STOP reference-model events as sampling points. Compare busy after each event is registered, and assert busy=0 during the pre-START interval and from the first cycle after detected STOP onward.

elements.stimulus: Perform a requirements-to-testplan traceability review for list item 8; do not apply any DUT stimulus or impose an expected functional behavior.
elements.expected_response: No requirement-specific DUT response is required or asserted for REQ-0070.
elements.check_method: Review the testplan traceability record and confirm that REQ-0070 is represented without any functional output comparison or additional behavioral obligation.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al cleared, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, and provide a released-high bus until the WRITE sequence reaches arbitration_checking with sda_oen=1. Then externally hold SDA low long enough for the synchronizer/filter reference model to produce filtered SDA low, and sample the next arbitration-checking clock edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the asserting side of the requirement: al asserts on the arbitration-checking edge where SDA is released high but filtered SDA is low. The command aborts without cmd_ack and the controller releases SDA and SCL.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and FSM reference model to identify the arbitration-checking edge and compare al against a transition from 0 to 1 on that edge; also check that cmd_ack remains low for the aborted command and both output enables are released after the abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al cleared, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, and provide SDA high externally while the WRITE sequence reaches arbitration_checking with sda_oen=1. Keep SDA high long enough for the filter reference model to produce filtered SDA high, and sample the arbitration-checking clock edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-asserting side of the requirement: al does not newly assert on the arbitration-checking edge because filtered SDA is not low; the WRITE sequence continues toward its normal completion and produces its ordinary cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and FSM reference model to identify the released-high arbitration-checking edge and assert that al remains 0 throughout the normal WRITE sequence, then verify exactly one cmd_ack at normal completion.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the bus initially released high, issue a READ command and wait until the read sample window is active with filtered SCL high and SDA released. Drive filtered SDA low, then hold SCL high and drive filtered SDA high long enough for the filter to detect a low-to-high transition, before the READ command completes.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for REQ-0072: the filtered STOP condition occurs while the bit-level FSM is active and the current command is READ, not STOP. The DUT shall assert al following STOP-condition detection.
elements.check_method: Use the active_command, in_read_sequence, read_sample_window, and stop_condition probes to qualify the event; compare al sampled after the detecting posedge against its prior value and require a 0-to-1 transition. Also verify the event is not merely a STOP observed while idle or during a requested STOP command.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the bus busy or otherwise valid for a STOP transaction, issue the STOP command and let the controller execute its STOP sequence until it releases SDA high while filtered SCL is high, producing the requested filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0072: although a STOP condition is detected while the bit-level FSM is active, the current command is the requested STOP command. The DUT shall not newly assert al as a result of this STOP condition.
elements.check_method: Use in_stop_sequence and stop_condition to qualify the requested STOP event; sample al after the detecting posedge and compare it with its value immediately before the event, requiring no 0-to-1 transition. Initialize al low and separately confirm that any pre-existing sticky al is not interpreted as newly asserted.

elements.stimulus: Set ena high and issue a WRITE command with din=1 while the bus is released high. Advance through the command until the WRITE stable-high arbitration-checking phase, then externally hold SDA low through sda_i while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: When arbitration loss is detected, al asserts. On the following registered response, in_idle is true and both scl_oen and sda_oen are high, which is the holding side of the observed_via shows: SCL and SDA are released after the FSM returns to idle.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the enabled timing and filtering to identify the filtered SDA-low arbitration event. At that event and the next settled posedge, sample al, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen; require al=1, in_idle=1, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1, and verify both enables remain high on subsequent idle clocks.

elements.stimulus: Set ena high and issue a normal WRITE command with din=0 on a bus that remains high and does not cause arbitration loss. Advance to the WRITE data-drive phase before the controller releases SCL for the high phase.
elements.expected_response: While the command is active, in_write_sequence is true and sda_oen is low to drive SDA low; therefore the observed port is on the contrasting, ordinary-command side of the observed_via shows rather than the arbitration-loss holding side. The FSM must not enter idle or assert al merely from this normal phase.
elements.check_method: Use the timing and FSM reference model to locate the WRITE data-drive phase. After the registered output update, require in_write_sequence=1, sda_oen=0, and al=0; separately confirm that the arbitration-loss expectation of both output enables high is not applied during this preceding ordinary command phase.

elements.stimulus: Apply no requirement-specific stimulus; record REQ-0074 as a scaffolding item whose text states that no requirement applies.
elements.expected_response: No output behavior, state transition, timing, or interface response is required by REQ-0074.
elements.check_method: Review the requirement-to-testplan traceability report and confirm the item is covered without imposing any DUT assertion or behavioral expectation.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ from idle with the bus released. During the resulting READ sampling window, drive sda_i so that the filtered SDA value is 0, then drive scl_i high long enough for the synchronizer/filter model to produce one filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when filtered_scl_rise and read_sample_window coincide, dout updates on the corresponding clock edge to the filtered SDA value 0.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization, filter majority, and filtered-edge timing; at each observed filtered_scl_rise while read_sample_window is asserted, compare the registered dout after the posedge with the model's filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ from idle with the bus released. Enter the READ sampling window, initialize dout to a known value, and keep scl_i low or otherwise prevent a filtered SCL rising edge while toggling sda_i, with each toggle shorter than required to change the filtered SCL state.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs during the READ sampling window, dout does not capture the toggled filtered SDA values and remains at its previously registered value.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model to prove that filtered_scl_rise remains deasserted throughout the sampling window, then assert that dout has no update on any clock in that interval despite SDA input activity.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted and al low, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while ena=1. During the resulting READ sampling window, drive the external bus so filtered SDA is 1 and filtered SCL transitions from low to high, producing one filtered SCL rising edge; repeat with filtered SDA equal to 0 on a subsequent READ bit if supported by the surrounding transaction.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: on each filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sampling window, dout captures the corresponding filtered SDA value, showing 1 for the first sampled bit and 0 for the subsequent sampled bit, with the registered update visible after the processing posedge.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronizer, filter majority value, filtered SCL edge detection, and registered dout timing. At every modeled filtered SCL rising edge while in_read_sequence/read_sample_window is asserted, compare post-posedge dout with the modeled filtered SDA value and record a bin for each captured value.

elements.stimulus: Initialize dout to 0, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while ena=1, and enter the READ sampling window. Change the external SDA input to 1 while keeping filtered SCL low so that no filtered SCL rising edge occurs during the interval; then end or abort the READ operation without providing a filtered SCL rising edge for that attempted data bit.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: dout does not capture the filtered SDA value 1 when no filtered SCL rising edge occurs during the READ sampling window; dout remains at its previously registered value of 0 until a valid qualifying sampling edge occurs.
elements.check_method: Reference-model the filtered SCL waveform and assert that no filtered_scl_rise event occurs while read_sample_window is active. Compare dout before and after the SDA transition and through command completion, requiring no dout update attributable to that unsampled bit.

elements.stimulus: Load the authoritative specification text and locate the command-FSM description identified by the specification.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the command-FSM description is explicitly labeled as item 10. No DUT port behavior is applicable because this requirement owns no port and has no observed_via mapping.
elements.check_method: Document-level assertion that the located command-FSM description has the exact item label "10."; record the result as the requirement-holds bin.

elements.stimulus: Evaluate a specification variant or extracted document in which the command-FSM description is unlabeled or labeled with an item number other than 10.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the command-FSM description is not labeled as item 10, so REQ-0077 does not hold. No DUT port behavior is expected to differ because the requirement has no observable port mapping.
elements.check_method: Document-level negative assertion that the command-FSM description lacks the exact item label "10."; record the result as the requirement-does-not-hold bin and confirm that no interface-level check is claimed.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, and issue cmd=START while idle. Use the divider reference model with a nonzero clk_cnt to identify the enabled timing tick that accepts START and each subsequent clk_en tick; keep cmd=START and the bus inputs stable through the command sequence.
elements.expected_response: At the modeled acceptance clk_en tick, the FSM leaves the idle output pattern and begins the START sequence, with registered sda_oen/scl_oen showing SDA driven low while SCL remains released. On the next modeled clk_en tick, the FSM advances to the following START phase, rather than changing phase on an intervening clock. This is the 'when the internal clk_en signal is asserted' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, compare in_idle/in_start_sequence and sda_oen/scl_oen against a reference FSM driven by the divider's modeled clk_en ticks. Assert that each command-phase transition occurs only on a cycle where the reference clk_en is 1, and that the expected START output trace begins after command acceptance.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, and issue cmd=START while idle. Select a clk_cnt value that creates multiple enabled-clock cycles between modeled clk_en ticks. After START is accepted on a modeled tick, hold all command and bus inputs stable and observe the intervening posedges before the next modeled clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: During every enabled clock between clk_en ticks, the FSM remains in the same START phase and registered sda_oen/scl_oen remain unchanged; it must not advance to the next START phase or produce a later-phase output pattern. This is the 'when the internal clk_en signal is not asserted' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the divider reference model to mark cycles with clk_en=0, sample in_start_sequence/in_idle and both output enables after each posedge, and compare consecutive non-tick cycles. Assert no FSM probe or output-enable transition occurs on a clk_en=0 cycle; then confirm the transition occurs at the next modeled clk_en=1 cycle.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold cmd=0001 (START) while the external SCL and SDA lines are released high, and provide enabled clocks through command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled timing opportunity while the FSM is idle, the FSM selects and executes the START sequence; cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at the sequence terminal phase and then returns low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after reset release, compare cmd_ack against a reference command-FSM model keyed by cmd=START and clk_en_tick; verify exactly one asserted sample and correlate it with the START output-enable phase sequence.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold cmd=0010 (STOP) while the external SCL line can be released high, and provide enabled clocks through command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled timing opportunity while the FSM is idle, the FSM selects and executes the STOP sequence; cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at the sequence terminal phase and then returns low.
elements.check_method: Use a reference FSM to predict the STOP sequence from the idle-state decode and compare the observed one-clock cmd_ack pulse and STOP output-enable ordering against that prediction.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold cmd=1000 (READ), drive the external SDA value during the read window, and provide enabled clocks through command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled timing opportunity while the FSM is idle, the FSM selects and executes the READ sequence; cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock after the read bit cycle completes and then returns low.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed cmd_ack timing and read output-enable sequence with a reference model that decodes cmd=READ on the idle clk_en_tick and advances through the read phases.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold cmd=0100 (WRITE), drive din to either 0 and then 1 in separate runs, and provide enabled clocks through command completion with SDA not causing arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled timing opportunity while the FSM is idle, the FSM selects and executes the WRITE sequence for the supplied din value; cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at completion and then returns low.
elements.check_method: For each din value, compare the observed SDA output-enable polarity, WRITE phase ordering, and single cmd_ack pulse against the reference model selected by cmd=WRITE.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold unsupported cmd=0011 while the FSM is reset-established idle, and provide multiple enabled clocks without changing cmd.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding contrast: no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE sequence is selected or completed, so cmd_ack remains low and does not pulse for the pending command.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack over the full observation window and compare it with a reference idle decoder; flag any one-clock completion pulse or command-sequence output-enable transition as a failure.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, clk_cnt=1, a released-high bus (scl_i=1, sda_i=1), and cmd=START (4'b0001) while the FSM is idle; keep inputs stable until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed shows: after command acceptance, scl_oen and sda_oen follow the START timing phases: both lines initially released, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released high (scl_oen=1, sda_oen=0), then SCL is driven low (scl_oen=0) before the sequence returns to idle and pulses cmd_ack for one clock.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use the in_start_sequence and in_idle probes plus a reference phase model to compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the required START sequence and verify the single cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Create a busy transaction context with a released-high bus, then drive ena=1, clk_cnt=1, and cmd=STOP (4'b0010) while the FSM is idle; keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 except as driven by the DUT until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed shows: during STOP, SDA is driven low, SCL is released high, and SDA is then released high while SCL remains released; the sequence returns to idle and produces one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the in_stop_sequence and in_idle probes and compare every settled scl_oen and sda_oen value at enabled timing ticks with a STOP reference model; check that cmd_ack is exactly one clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=READ (4'b1000), scl_i=1, and sda_i=0 or 1; hold the command and bus inputs through completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed shows: during the READ sequence, sda_oen remains released so the slave can drive SDA, while scl_oen transitions from the low phase to released high for the read window and then back to driven low before cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use in_read_sequence and read_sample_window to align sampled registered outputs with the READ reference model; compare scl_oen and sda_oen on every phase boundary and verify completion with one cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), and a released-high bus; keep the bus externally high and hold inputs until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed shows: during WRITE of din=0, sda_oen is driven low for the data phase, scl_oen is then released high for the stable high phase, and scl_oen is driven low again before the FSM returns idle and pulses cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and arbitration_checking probes with a WRITE reference model; compare the registered scl_oen and sda_oen phase values and verify no arbitration loss and one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=1, cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), and a released-high bus with sda_i=1; hold inputs until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed shows: during WRITE of din=1, sda_oen is released for the data phase, scl_oen is released high for the stable high phase, and scl_oen is driven low again before idle and a one-clock cmd_ack; no arbitration loss occurs while the observed SDA remains high.
elements.check_method: Use in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and arbitration_checking to identify the phases; compare scl_oen and sda_oen with the din=1 reference model and check al remains low and cmd_ack occurs once.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and the bus released high, drive cmd=NOP (4'b0000) while idle, then repeat with unsupported cmd values 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0111, and 4'b1111; hold each value for multiple enabled timing ticks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting 'otherwise' case of the observed shows: because no recognized command sequence is active, scl_oen and sda_oen remain at the released idle pair (1,1), neither output enable performs a START, STOP, READ, or WRITE phase transition, and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge, use in_idle to confirm the FSM remains idle and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against the released idle values; assert that no phase transition or cmd_ack occurs for any tested no-op encoding.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=START on an enabled clk_en tick with scl_i and sda_i initially high; provide the expected released-high, SDA-low, and SCL-low bus phases until the START sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0081: on completion of the START sequence, in_idle becomes asserted and cmd_ack becomes high for exactly one clock cycle, then returns low while in_idle remains asserted.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate FSM/timing reference model synchronized to posedge clk. At the modeled terminal phase, assert in_idle and cmd_ack together, require cmd_ack to be high on exactly one sampled clock and low on the next, and require no additional pulse.

elements.stimulus: With the bus busy from a completed START, set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP on an enabled clk_en tick; allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL high, and release SDA while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0081: at the STOP terminal phase, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock cycle, followed by cmd_ack low; the STOP sequence is not left active.
elements.check_method: Compare in_idle and cmd_ack against a variable-latency reference model that accounts for clk_en and filtered bus timing. Assert the terminal-cycle idle/ack pair and use a one-cycle pulse-width assertion for cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, din=0, and issue cmd=WRITE on an enabled clk_en tick with the external bus releasing SDA high whenever the DUT releases it; allow the write sequence through its released-SCL high phase and subsequent SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0081: when the WRITE sequence completes, in_idle is asserted and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle, then cmd_ack is low and the FSM remains idle.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the WRITE terminal phase independent of prescaler latency. Sample registered outputs after each posedge and assert in_idle at completion, a single-cycle cmd_ack pulse, and no later acknowledgement without another accepted command.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ on an enabled clk_en tick; release SDA externally, provide a filtered SCL rising edge with SDA high, then allow the read sequence to pull SCL low and reach its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0081: after the READ low phase completes, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle; cmd_ack is low on all following clocks.
elements.check_method: Drive and monitor the filtered-SCL reference model, identify the READ terminal phase after the captured bit, and assert the simultaneous in_idle assertion and one-clock cmd_ack pulse at that phase.

elements.stimulus: While in_idle with ena=1, issue cmd=0000 and each unsupported 4-bit encoding other than 0001, 0010, 0100, and 1000, holding the bus lines stable and observing several enabled clocks for each value.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0081: no supported command sequence or terminal phase is entered, so cmd_ack remains low for every clock and in_idle remains asserted; the one-clock terminal acknowledgement behavior is not produced.
elements.check_method: Enumerate all unsupported cmd values and assert that no in_idle deassertion, command-phase probe activation, or cmd_ack pulse occurs during a bounded observation window. Distinguish this ordinary idle behavior from the positive terminal-phase checks.

elements.stimulus: Apply no DUT stimulus; review the specification and requirement traceability for list item 11.
elements.expected_response: No behavioral assertion, input condition, output value, timing constraint, or coverage bin is required for REQ-0082.
elements.check_method: Static requirement-audit check confirming the item remains classified as scaffolding with expectation 'no behavioral obligation' and has no DUT-facing verification criterion.
