elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with the bus externally released high, set ena=1, choose a nonzero clk_cnt such as 1, then issue cmd=START (4'b0001) while the command FSM is idle. Continue clocking with ena=1 and keep SCL/SDA externally released so the START sequence can complete.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of the observed behavior: after START acceptance, sda_oen and scl_oen are both high (released); the sequence then drives SDA low by setting sda_oen low while scl_oen remains high; it subsequently drives SCL low by setting scl_oen low; after that transition cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clock. The output-enable ordering is release both, SDA low with SCL released, then SCL low.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked assertion or reference-model comparison sampled after each posedge and NBA settling. Record the sda_oen/scl_oen/cmd_ack waveform from command acceptance through completion and require the ordered phases, with cmd_ack high for one cycle only after scl_oen becomes low; require no earlier cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with the bus externally released high, set ena=1, choose the same clk_cnt value used in the positive case, and issue cmd=NOP (4'b0000) while the command FSM is idle. Continue clocking for at least the full latency window used by the START test without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of the observed behavior: because no START command is accepted, sda_oen and scl_oen remain released high and do not show the START-specific transition of SDA low while SCL remains high followed by SCL low; cmd_ack remains low. In particular, no START completion pulse is produced.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked waveform monitor and reference model over the same observation window as TP-0000. Assert that sda_oen never transitions low, scl_oen never transitions low, and cmd_ack is never high while the FSM remains idle.

elements.stimulus: Encounter the source specification's list-item number 12; apply no DUT stimulus because the item declares no required behavior.
elements.expected_response: No DUT response is required or constrained by this requirement.
elements.check_method: Review the requirement traceability record and confirm that the item is classified as having no behavioral obligation; perform no interface comparison.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus externally released high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue cmd=0010 (STOP) on a clock edge, then continue providing enabled clocks until the STOP sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0085: during the STOP sequence, sda_oen first becomes 0 while scl_oen is low or remains in its pre-STOP state, then scl_oen becomes 1 to release SCL, and finally sda_oen becomes 1 while scl_oen remains 1. The observed ordering is SDA driven low, SCL released high, then SDA released high while SCL is high.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge, record scl_oen and sda_oen and use a temporal checker requiring the ordered phases sda_oen=0, then scl_oen=1, then sda_oen=1 with scl_oen still 1; require no final SDA release before SCL release.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the bus externally released high, keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue cmd=0000 (NOP) while idle, and observe several enabled clock cycles without issuing START, STOP, READ, or WRITE.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of REQ-0085: scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the idle released state and do not show the STOP-specific sequence of SDA driven low followed by SCL release and then SDA release while SCL remains released. In particular, no STOP ordering is observable.
elements.check_method: Monitor the output-enable trace over the observation window and assert that no subsequence sda_oen=0 -> scl_oen=1 -> sda_oen=1 with scl_oen continuously 1 occurs; compare against the STOP temporal signature used in TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: From idle with ena=1, drive cmd=0010 (STOP) on an enabled timing tick. Model the bus released high so the STOP sequence can drive SDA low, release SCL high, and then reach the final phase with scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: When the STOP sequence reaches the final SDA-release phase, both scl_oen and sda_oen are 1 and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock. This is the holding side of the observed behavior: cmd_ack asserts after SDA is released high while SCL is high.
elements.check_method: Use the STOP reference-model state and in_stop_sequence probe to identify the final SDA-release phase; sample registered outputs after each posedge, assert scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1 in that phase, and compare cmd_ack against a one-clock expected pulse immediately following completion.

elements.stimulus: From idle with ena=1, issue cmd=0010 (STOP), allow the sequence to drive SDA low and release SCL high, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the FSM reaches the final phase that releases SDA high.
elements.expected_response: The STOP sequence is aborted and reset releases both output enables, but the final SDA-release completion phase is not reached and cmd_ack does not assert after the aborted STOP. This is the contrasting side of the observed behavior: without the completed final release phase, cmd_ack does not assert.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_stop_sequence and sda_oen to confirm reset occurs before the final SDA-release phase; asynchronously check reset initialization, then sample cmd_ack for the remainder of the aborted command and require no pulse.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, then set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) while the controller is idle. Provide a released bus with sda_i=1 and scl_i=1, and continue clocking through the enabled timing ticks until the READ data-bit sequence is active and before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the READ data-bit sequence, sda_oen is 1: this is the 'shows' side indicating that SDA is released for the slave to drive.
elements.check_method: At every posedge while in_read_sequence is asserted and before cmd_ack, sample sda_oen after registered outputs settle and compare it against 1; record a bin for the READ release phase and fail if any sampled value is 0.

elements.stimulus: From idle with ena=1, issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=0 on an enabled timing tick. Hold the external bus high and continue clocking until the WRITE data-bit phase is active.
elements.expected_response: During the contrasting non-READ WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 0, i.e. sda_oen is not 1; the controller owns SDA and drives it low rather than releasing it for a slave.
elements.check_method: While in_write_sequence is asserted before command completion, sample sda_oen after each posedge and compare it against 0. Cross-check that this contrasting phase is not in_read_sequence and that the observed value is the 'otherwise' side of the REQ-0087 port observation.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b1000 (READ) while the bus is released high. Allow the READ command to be accepted from idle and use the timing/filter reference model to identify entry into the READ sample window; keep the external SCL and SDA lines released so the filtered SCL can rise.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the observed behavior: throughout the READ sample window, scl_oen remains 1, releasing SCL high.
elements.check_method: Use the read_sample_window probe and sample scl_oen after each settled posedge. Assert scl_oen==1 on every cycle for which read_sample_window is active; record a bin for READ sample-window release.

elements.stimulus: Run the same enabled READ transaction with cmd=4'b1000 and a released bus. After the filtered SCL rising edge opens the READ sample window, allow the controller's modeled sample-window timing to complete and continue clocking until the READ phase exits.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting side of the observed behavior: when the READ sample window ends, scl_oen becomes 0 and SCL is driven low; it must not remain released high after the window.
elements.check_method: Monitor read_sample_window, filtered_scl_rise, and scl_oen after settled posedges. Check that scl_oen is 1 during the window and that the first state transition ending the window is followed by scl_oen==0, with no intervening unexpected release; record a bin for the high-to-low sample-window transition.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and present cmd=READ (1000) while idle. Allow the enabled timing tick to enter the READ sequence, with sda_oen released and scl_oen released for the READ sample window. Drive the bus so filtered SDA is 0, then cause filtered SCL to transition from low to high and produce filtered_scl_rise=1.
elements.expected_response: During the READ sample window, at the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 0, the current filtered SDA value. This is the holding case described by observed_via.shows.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization, filtering, and READ sequencing. At the posedge that observes filtered_scl_rise during read_sample_window, compare the settled registered dout value with filtered SDA and require dout==0; also verify the update occurs only at that sampling edge.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT and leave it idle with ena=1 and cmd=NOP. Initialize dout to a known value, drive the filtered bus so filtered SDA has a defined value, and cause a filtered SCL rising edge while read_sample_window=0, such as during idle or a non-READ phase. Do not issue a READ command.
elements.expected_response: Because the filtered SCL rising edge is outside the READ sample window, dout does not update from this event and retains its prior value. This is the contrasting otherwise case described by observed_via.shows.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered_scl_rise and read_sample_window in the reference model; on each rising edge with read_sample_window=0, compare dout before and after the settled posedge and require no change, regardless of filtered SDA.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) on an enabled timing tick, keep the bus available, release SDA for the READ window, drive the external SDA line to 0, and provide a filtered SCL rising edge followed by the normal low phase.
elements.expected_response: After the filtered SCL rising edge, dout captures 0; when the READ terminal phase completes, cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock. This is the positive side of observed_via.shows: cmd_ack pulses high to indicate that the READ command has ended.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for clk_en, filtering, READ phases, and filtered SCL rising-edge detection. At the registered outputs after each posedge, compare dout at the filtered rising edge and assert that exactly one cmd_ack cycle occurs after capture and before return to idle, with cmd_ack low on adjacent cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) on an enabled timing tick. Allow the READ sample window to reach a filtered SCL rising edge and drive a valid external SDA value so dout is captured, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the READ terminal phase can complete; deassert nReset and continue clocking.
elements.expected_response: The reset aborts the pending READ command, returns the controller to idle, and no cmd_ack pulse is produced for that READ. This is the contrasting side of observed_via.shows: when the terminal completion condition is aborted before it is reached, cmd_ack does not provide a completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered SCL rising-edge probe and dout to confirm sampling occurred, then check cmd_ack on every clock from reset assertion through subsequent recovery; require no high pulse associated with the aborted command and verify idle recovery after reset.

elements.stimulus: Apply a representative idle-cycle stimulus with ena low and high, cmd=N​​OP, arbitrary clk_cnt, din, scl_i, and sda_i values, without asserting either reset.
elements.expected_response: No output behavior is required by REQ-0091; the test must not impose or report any pass/fail expectation on cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, or sda_oen.
elements.check_method: Review the generated test result and assertion set to confirm that the scenario is recorded as covered while containing no DUT behavioral assertions or output comparisons.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, present cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), set din=0, and keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high. Hold cmd and din stable until the WRITE command is accepted, then continue supplying enabled clocks through command completion.
elements.expected_response: For the din=0 holding case, sda_oen is 0 during the WRITE data-bit phase, driving SDA low. The controller then sets scl_oen=1 to release SCL high, asserts arbitration_checking during that released-high phase, and subsequently sets scl_oen=0 to drive SCL low.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block scoreboard sampled after each posedge. On the in_write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase probes, compare sda_oen against 0 for din=0, require scl_oen to transition 0-to-1-to-0 in the WRITE phase order, and require arbitration_checking to overlap the scl_oen=1 interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, present cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), set din=1, and keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high. Hold cmd and din stable until the WRITE command is accepted, then continue supplying enabled clocks through command completion.
elements.expected_response: For the din=1 contrasting case, sda_oen is 1 during the WRITE data-bit phase, releasing SDA. The controller then sets scl_oen=1 to release SCL high, asserts arbitration_checking during that released-high phase, and subsequently sets scl_oen=0 to drive SCL low.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block scoreboard sampled after each posedge. On the in_write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase probes, compare sda_oen against 1 for din=1, require scl_oen to transition 0-to-1-to-0 in the WRITE phase order, and require arbitration_checking to overlap the scl_oen=1 interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus released, present cmd=0100 (WRITE) while idle with din=0, and provide filtered SCL responses that allow the WRITE sequence to complete through its released high phase and terminal low-SCL phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the end of the active WRITE sequence, after the terminal low-SCL phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock and then returns low.
elements.check_method: Use a clock-sampled assertion triggered by WRITE acceptance that waits for the modeled terminal low-SCL phase, then require cmd_ack==1 for exactly one posedge and cmd_ack==0 on the following posedge; flag any missing or multi-clock pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and present cmd=0100 (WRITE) while idle with din=1; allow the command to enter its released-high arbitration-checking phase, then externally hold SDA low so arbitration loss is detected before the terminal low-SCL completion phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: cmd_ack does not pulse at the end of the WRITE sequence because the WRITE is aborted by arbitration loss; the command returns to the released idle condition.
elements.check_method: Monitor the clock-sampled arbitration-loss event and assert that no cmd_ack high pulse occurs from that event through the remainder of the aborted command; require both output enables to be released after abort.

elements.stimulus: Provide the current specification artifact containing the item referenced by REQ-0094.
elements.expected_response: The specification artifact labels the following item as item 15.
elements.check_method: Parse the specification source around the pinned obligation span and compare the item label against the expected value 15; record a pass only when the label is present and exact.

elements.stimulus: Initialize the controller, start a command so the FSM is non-idle, then assert nReset=0 between clk rising edges while ena=1 and the external SCL/SDA lines are released.
elements.expected_response: Immediately when nReset is asserted low, the FSM enters idle, scl_oen and sda_oen become high, and cmd_ack, al, and busy become low. Counters and filter state reset, and filtered SCL/SDA initialize high.
elements.check_method: Use asynchronous waveform checks immediately after the nReset transition, plus probes for in_idle and filter_sample_event/reference-model state; assert exact values scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0 and initialized filtered-line values high without waiting for a clk edge.

elements.stimulus: After releasing nReset, issue a valid WRITE command with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, and released external bus lines; allow the command to progress through its enabled timing phases.
elements.expected_response: Outside reset, the ordinary command behavior is observed: during the active WRITE phase sda_oen becomes low to drive SDA low and the FSM is not idle; the command later returns idle and produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack. Thus scl_oen/sda_oen are not required to remain high outside reset.
elements.check_method: Sample registered outputs after each posedge and correlate them with in_write_sequence and in_idle; require sda_oen=0 during the WRITE drive phase and a single cmd_ack pulse at completion. This is the contrasting, non-reset side of the scl_oen/sda_oen shows statements.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1 and an active command or nonzero status established, assert rst=1 before a clk rising edge and hold it through that edge; keep nReset deasserted.
elements.expected_response: Before the applying rising edge, synchronous reset has not yet taken effect. On the next rising edge, the FSM enters idle, scl_oen and sda_oen become high, cmd_ack, al, and busy become low, counters and filter state reset, and filtered SCL/SDA initialize high.
elements.check_method: Check outputs both immediately before the reset-applying posedge and after NBA updates at that posedge. Use in_idle and a reference model for counters/filter histories; require reset values only at the applying edge, distinguishing synchronous reset from asynchronous reset.

elements.stimulus: Release rst and nReset, then issue a valid WRITE command with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, and released external bus lines; observe the active command before completion.
elements.expected_response: When neither reset is asserted, ordinary behavior resumes rather than holding reset values: the FSM becomes active, sda_oen becomes low for the din=0 WRITE bit, and cmd_ack remains low until the command terminal phase, after which the FSM returns idle and pulses cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Compare post-reset registered waveforms against the command reference model and in_write_sequence/in_idle probes; verify the contrasting non-reset behavior at scl_oen/sda_oen and cmd_ack rather than treating reset values as permanent.

elements.stimulus: Inspect the source specification and confirm that the section beginning at the cited Processing Flow span is labeled exactly "Processing Flow"; run the DUT with reset released and no command activity.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the specification contains the required "Processing Flow" label. No DUT output is required to change because this documentation condition has no DUT-visible effect; all observed DUT outputs remain at their ordinary idle values.
elements.check_method: Perform an exact-text document assertion for the heading, then compare the DUT trace against an idle reference model for cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_o, sda_o, scl_oen, and sda_oen.

elements.stimulus: Use a controlled negative copy of the source specification in which the cited section label is removed or changed from "Processing Flow"; run the same DUT idle stimulus with reset released and no command activity.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the specification does not contain the required "Processing Flow" label. The DUT must still show the same ordinary idle outputs as in the holding case, because no DUT port distinguishes whether this documentation label exists.
elements.check_method: Assert that the negative document copy lacks the exact heading, then perform a differential comparison of all observed DUT outputs against TP-0000 and the idle reference model; require no DUT-visible difference.

elements.stimulus: While clk is running, assert nReset=0 between clock edges, then keep nReset=0 through at least one clock edge. Deassert nReset while holding rst=0, ena=0, and cmd=NOP before any normal command processing.
elements.expected_response: The reset-first side of REQ-0097 is satisfied: scl_oen becomes high asynchronously when nReset is asserted and remains high after reset initialization, indicating that SCL is released before normal processing begins.
elements.check_method: Use an asynchronous monitor to sample scl_oen immediately after nReset assertion, then sample after the next posedge and after nReset deassertion. Assert scl_oen==1 at each reset-initialized observation and before issuing any command.

elements.stimulus: Start with nReset=1 and rst=0, do not apply either reset before normal processing, and drive ena=1 with cmd=START and a released-high external bus on successive clock edges.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting, not-reset-initialized side of REQ-0097 applies: before reset initialization has occurred, scl_oen is not required to show the reset-initialized released value high. A high scl_oen observation in this condition must not be counted as evidence that reset-and-initialization processing occurred first; the checker shall not impose a reset-initialized scl_oen requirement on this pre-reset sequence.
elements.check_method: Run with four-state signal observation and record whether reset was ever asserted before the first command. For the command-before-reset interval, ensure the checker applies no assertion requiring scl_oen==1 as reset evidence; separately flag any testbench or reference-model assumption that normal processing was preceded by reset.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue a valid START command with the bus released and clk_cnt=1. After the in_start_sequence probe becomes asserted, drive nReset=0 asynchronously between clock edges and hold it low through at least one clock edge.
elements.expected_response: While the asynchronous reset is asserted, the command FSM returns to the known idle state: in_idle becomes asserted. This is the reset-holding side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At an observation point after nReset falls and after registered state settles, compare in_idle against 1'b1; also confirm it remains asserted through the next clock edge.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue a valid START command with the bus released and clk_cnt=1. Wait until in_start_sequence is asserted, deassert nReset, then set rst=1 before a rising edge and hold rst high across that rising edge.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge with synchronous rst asserted, the command FSM returns to the known idle state and in_idle becomes asserted. This is the synchronous-reset holding side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample in_idle after nonblocking assignments settle on the reset clock edge and compare it against 1'b1; verify the probe remains asserted while rst stays high.

elements.stimulus: Set nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, and issue a valid START command with the bus released and clk_cnt=1. While in_start_sequence is asserted, do not assert either reset input and observe the next enabled command-timing interval.
elements.expected_response: Without either reset activation, the controller retains its active command behavior and does not return to the known idle state at that observation point: in_idle remains deasserted. This is the contrasting non-reset side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the in_start_sequence and in_idle probes after each enabled timing interval; require in_start_sequence=1 and in_idle=0 before command completion, contrasting with the reset cases.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, rst low, ena high, clk_cnt set to 1, and the bus released high, issue a START command and wait until the command FSM is active. Assert nReset low between two rising edges of clk and keep it low for at least one clock period.
elements.expected_response: Immediately upon asynchronous reset assertion, the FSM returns to idle; cmd_ack, busy, and al are low; scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing SCL and SDA; arbitration checking is disabled; counters are reset or reloaded; and the filtered SCL/SDA state is initialized to idle-high.
elements.check_method: Sample registered outputs after the asynchronous reset event and confirm cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. Check in_idle=1 and arbitration_checking=0 with probes, and compare divider, filter-history, and filtered-line state against the reset reference model.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, rst low, ena high, clk_cnt set to 1, and the bus released high, issue a WRITE command with din=0 and wait until the FSM is active. Assert rst high before a rising edge of clk, then provide that rising edge while keeping rst high.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge that samples rst high, the FSM returns to idle; cmd_ack, busy, and al are low; scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing SCL and SDA; arbitration checking is disabled; counters are reset or reloaded; and the filtered SCL/SDA state is initialized to idle-high.
elements.check_method: After nonblocking assignments settle on the reset-sampling rising edge, compare cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1 against the expected reset values. Check in_idle=1 and arbitration_checking=0 with probes, and compare counter, filter-history, and filtered-line state against the synchronous-reset reference model.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset high and rst low, set ena high and clk_cnt to 1, hold the bus released high, then issue a valid WRITE command with din=0 while no reset is asserted. Allow the command to progress through its low phase, released-high phase, and terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Outside reset, the module follows ordinary command behavior rather than reset behavior: the FSM becomes active, sda_oen is low while driving din=0, scl_oen is released during the high phase, and cmd_ack eventually pulses for one clock when the WRITE completes; outputs are not forced continuously to the reset state during the active command.
elements.check_method: Use in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and active_command probes to identify command phases. At each phase compare scl_oen and sda_oen to the WRITE reference model, and verify exactly one cmd_ack pulse at completion. Confirm that the observed active-command behavior is the non-reset side of the port distinction.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it between clocks, keep rst low, set ena high, and hold scl_i and sda_i high through reset initialization. Then drive a valid START by keeping scl_i high and transitioning sda_i from high to low, holding the levels long enough to pass the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample majority filter.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: busy becomes 1 after the filtered START is recognized, demonstrating that post-reset sampling of scl_i and sda_i is active. The contrasting failure condition is busy remaining 0 after the valid filtered START.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronizer, filter history, and filtered START detection; compare the model's START event and expected busy transition against the registered busy output after nonblocking assignments settle.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it between clocks, keep rst low, set ena high, hold scl_i and sda_i high, then drive a valid filtered START to establish busy=1. Subsequently keep scl_i high and transition sda_i from low to high for a valid STOP, holding the levels long enough to pass synchronization and majority filtering.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: busy clears to 0 after the filtered STOP is recognized, demonstrating continued post-reset sampling and processing of sda_i while scl_i is high. The contrasting failure condition is busy remaining 1 after the valid filtered STOP.
elements.check_method: Run the synchronizer/filter reference model to predict the filtered STOP event, then compare the predicted registered busy clear with the DUT busy output on the corresponding settled clock edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a READ command with ena high. During the read window, hold scl_i high and hold sda_i at 1 for enough rising edges of clk for the value to be captured by both cSDA stages and propagated through the input filter. Then allow the filtered SCL rising edge to occur.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 1. This is the holding case of the observed behavior: dout captures the filtered SDA value corresponding to sda_i after the raw input has propagated through the two-stage capture and filter.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the cSCL/cSDA two-stage sampling and filter history. Detect filtered_scl_rise and compare the post-posedge dout value with the model's filtered SDA value; require dout=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a READ command with ena high and initialize the read sampling interval with sda_i=0. Keep sda_i=0 until too late before the expected filtered SCL rising edge, then change sda_i to 1 so that the transition cannot be captured and propagated through both synchronizer stages and the filter before that edge.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising edge, dout remains 0 rather than reflecting the late raw sda_i transition. This is the non-holding case of the observed behavior: a transition too late to be captured and filtered before the sampling edge does not affect dout.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to determine whether the late sda_i transition has reached the filtered SDA value by filtered_scl_rise. Compare dout after the sampling posedge with the prior/model filtered value and require dout=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and choose clk_cnt=0 for enabled-clock progress. Hold sda_i at a stable value of 1 for at least the complete two-stage synchronizer and filter latency before issuing a READ command. Provide a released-high SCL phase long enough to produce a filtered SCL rising edge, then complete the read low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of REQ-0102: dout captures the stable SDA value of 1 on the registered response to the filtered SCL rising edge. The captured value must agree with the synchronized and filtered SDA path, not with an unsynchronized transient.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage scl_i/sda_i capture, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered SCL edge detection. At the filtered SCL rising-edge event, compare dout after the posedge with the model's filtered SDA value and confirm the value has been stable through the modeled capture and filtering latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and choose clk_cnt=0. Hold sda_i at 0, issue a READ command, and arrange for the released SCL phase to produce a filtered SCL rising edge. Change raw sda_i from 0 to 1 less than two clocked capture stages plus the required filtering latency before that filtered SCL rising edge, while keeping the bus otherwise valid.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding side of REQ-0102: dout must not reflect the newly changed raw sda_i=1 at that read sampling edge. It must retain the previously captured/filtered SDA value of 0, or otherwise match the reference model's value based only on samples that completed the specified two-stage capture and filtering path. A dout value of 1 before that path completes indicates use of the raw bus signal and fails the requirement.
elements.check_method: Timestamp the raw sda_i transition relative to clk and the filtered SCL rising edge. Predict dout with a cycle-accurate two-stage synchronizer and filter model, then compare the registered dout after the edge. Flag any result that follows the raw transition earlier than the modeled capture and filtering latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the bus filtered idle high, set ena high and hold filtered SCL high. Drive SDA high-to-low for less than the filter qualification window, then return SDA high before the three-sample filter can qualify the transition.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding side of the busy observation: busy remains low, because the short SDA glitch does not pass the digital input filter and must not be recognized as a START condition.
elements.check_method: Monitor filter_sample_event, start_condition, and busy over the synchronized and filtered response window; assert that no start_condition occurs and busy never rises.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy low, set ena high and hold filtered SCL high. Drive SDA high-to-low and keep it low for at least the filter qualification interval so the captured samples produce a sustained filtered SDA transition.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the busy observation: the sustained transition passes through the digital input filter, produces a filtered START condition, and busy rises after the registered detection update.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to predict the filtered SDA transition; compare start_condition and the subsequent registered busy value, requiring busy to rise only after the qualified filtered transition.

elements.stimulus: Issue a READ command on an enabled clk_en tick, wait until the read_sample_window is active with SDA held at logic 1, initialize or confirm dout is 0, then apply an SCL low-to-high pulse shorter than the filter qualification window and return SCL low.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding side of the dout observation: dout remains 0 and is not updated, because the short SCL pulse does not pass the digital input filter and must not create a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Monitor filter_sample_event, filtered_scl_rise, read_sample_window, and dout; assert that no filtered_scl_rise is generated for the short pulse and dout remains unchanged.

elements.stimulus: Issue a READ command on an enabled clk_en tick, wait until the read_sample_window is active, hold external SDA at logic 1, and drive SCL low-to-high long enough for the captured samples to qualify a sustained filtered SCL rising transition.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the dout observation: the sustained SCL transition passes through the digital input filter, creates a filtered SCL rising edge, and dout updates to 1 on the registered sampling update.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to predict the qualified filtered SCL rising edge; compare filtered_scl_rise and dout, requiring dout to become 1 only on the registered update associated with that filtered edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset completes, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, hold filtered SCL high by driving scl_i=1, and hold sda_i=1 long enough for synchronizer and filter histories to settle. Then drive sda_i=0 stably and continue clocking until busy changes. Use a reference model with filter sample interval floor(8/4)=2 enabled clocks, including the two-stage synchronization and three-sample majority-filter settling.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for REQ-0104: busy asserts only after SDA has been sampled at the two-enabled-clock filter cadence and the majority-filtered SDA transition is detected. The measured latency must agree with the reference model and must not match an unshifted interval of 8 or continuous sampling.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare busy and the measured assertion cycle against a cycle-accurate reference model for the synchronizers, filter counter reload, three-sample histories, majority output, and START detection. Record a coverage bin for clk_cnt=8 and the predicted filter interval of 2.

elements.stimulus: After reset completes, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then drive sda_i=0. Sample busy at every enabled clock during the interval before the reference model's earliest possible filtered START detection, namely before the synchronized samples have been shifted at the floor(8/4)=2-clock cadence and the majority history has settled.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding side of the observation: busy must remain deasserted at every early checkpoint. An assertion caused by using an unshifted prescaler, a different shift, or continuous filter sampling is a failure because it is inconsistent with the required floor(clk_cnt/4) cadence.
elements.check_method: Use the same cycle-accurate filter reference model to calculate the earliest legal busy assertion. Assert busy==0 before that cycle and flag any earlier assertion; also compare the first assertion cycle against the model to distinguish the required cadence from continuous or incorrectly scaled sampling.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 asynchronously, release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, set clk_cnt=8, and drive stable scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Run posedge clk cycles while tracking the synchronized samples and filter counter with a reference model until the filter counter reaches its expiration point.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled cycle where the filter counter expires, filter_sample_event is asserted. This is the 'shows' asserted side: new synchronized SCL and SDA samples are shifted into the fSCL and fSDA three-sample histories.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare filter_sample_event with the reference model's filter-counter-expiration prediction and record a bin for an asserted expiration event. If filter-history probes are available, also compare their updates with the synchronized samples on that cycle.

elements.stimulus: Using the same enabled configuration with rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=8, and stable scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, select an enabled posedge after a filter sample event but before the reference-model filter counter reaches its next expiration point, and continue applying the stable inputs.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled non-expiration cycle, filter_sample_event remains deasserted. This is the 'shows' deasserted side: no new synchronized samples are shifted into the fSCL and fSDA histories because the filter counter has not expired.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare filter_sample_event against the reference model and require it to be 0 for a cycle predicted not to expire; ensure the filter-history values do not update due to a filter sample on that cycle.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then use the reference model to drive raw SCL low until filtered SCL is low. At a filter_sample_event, drive raw SCL and SDA so that the next synchronized histories become SCL={0,1,1} and SDA={0,1,1}, producing a 2-of-3 filtered SCL rising majority and a 2-of-3 filtered SDA high majority.
elements.expected_response: This is the majority-holds side of the dout observation: when the resulting filtered SCL rising edge is processed, dout updates to 1, the majority value of the three-sample SDA history, rather than to any isolated SDA sample.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter sample boundaries, history shifts, and majority function; at filtered_scl_rise compare dout with the modeled SDA majority and verify dout=1.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish filtered SCL low, then drive raw inputs so the next filter-sample boundary produces SCL={0,1,1} and SDA={0,0,1}; the isolated SDA high sample must not form a majority.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-majority side of the dout observation: the filtered SCL rising edge is processed, but dout updates to 0, the SDA-history majority, and does not reflect the isolated high SDA sample.
elements.check_method: Predict the synchronized histories and majority outputs with the reference model, detect the modeled filtered_scl_rise, and compare the registered dout value against the modeled SDA majority; verify dout=0.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset so busy=0, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high, then drive raw SDA low long enough that a filter-sample boundary produces an SDA history {1,1,0} while the SCL history remains high.
elements.expected_response: This is the majority-holds side of the busy observation: the 2-of-3 SDA high-to-low majority with filtered SCL high produces a qualified START, and busy changes from 0 to 1 after the registered detection update.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm the SDA majority transition and filtered SCL-high condition, observe the start_condition probe, and compare busy before and after the corresponding posedge; require busy=1 only for the qualified transition.

elements.stimulus: With busy=1, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and filtered SCL high, drive raw SDA high long enough that a filter-sample boundary produces an SDA history {0,0,1} while the SCL history remains high.
elements.expected_response: This is the majority-holds side of the busy observation for STOP: the 2-of-3 SDA low-to-high majority produces a qualified STOP, and busy changes from 1 to 0 after the registered detection update.
elements.check_method: Model the synchronized histories and majority outputs, observe the stop_condition probe at the qualifying sample boundary, and compare the registered busy transition on the following settled clock state; require busy=0.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish filtered SCL high and busy=0, then inject an SDA transition that causes only one of three synchronized samples to be low, yielding SDA history {1,0,1}; do not allow two low samples in the history.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-majority side of the busy observation: the isolated SDA transition does not produce a majority-filtered START or STOP, busy remains unchanged at 0, and no start_condition, stop_condition, or status change is generated from that sample.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to verify the SDA history has fewer than two samples of the transitioned value and filtered SCL is high; monitor start_condition, stop_condition, and busy across the sample boundary and require no event and no busy transition.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, hold filtered SCL high, and drive SDA stably high-to-low long enough for the synchronizer and three-sample majority filter to produce a filtered START; then drive SDA stably low-to-high while filtered SCL remains high long enough to produce a filtered STOP.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy is set after the filtered START and remains set while the bus is active, then busy is cleared after the filtered STOP. The changes occur only after the corresponding filtered transitions, demonstrating that filtered SCL and SDA are treated as the stable internal bus signals.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample majority values, and START/STOP edge detection. Compare the model's filtered transitions and expected busy set/clear events with the registered busy output after each settled posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and filtered SCL high, establish SDA high and busy low. Apply a raw SDA low pulse shorter than the interval required to change the three-sample majority-filtered SDA value, return SDA high, and repeat with a raw SCL glitch if needed without allowing either filtered signal to transition.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because the raw glitches do not change the majority-filtered SCL or SDA values, no filtered START or STOP is produced and busy remains unchanged at its pre-glitch value.
elements.check_method: Model the filter histories and majority outputs cycle by cycle, confirm that no filtered START/STOP transition occurs, and assert that busy has no transition throughout and after each injected glitch.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, and clk_cnt set to a nonzero value, apply a valid filtered START by holding SCL high and driving SDA high-to-low long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to settle. Then hold filtered SCL high and filtered SDA low for multiple filter sampling intervals without any further bus transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: after busy becomes 1 for the filtered START, busy remains 1 on every subsequent clock while the current filtered SCL/SDA values remain equal to their delayed dSCL/dSDA values and no new START or STOP transition is detected.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronizers, filter histories, filtered SCL/SDA, and delayed dSCL/dSDA. After the START is processed, compare busy after each enabled clock for several filter intervals against the model's retained value of 1; flag any change without a modeled filtered transition.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, and the bus initially filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high, drive SDA high-to-low and hold it long enough to produce a filtered START. After busy becomes 1, hold SDA low while SCL remains high, then drive SDA low-to-high and hold it long enough to produce a filtered STOP.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of the observed behavior: busy changes to 1 after the filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high, then changes to 0 after the filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high. These changes must occur only after the delayed filtered values expose the corresponding transitions.
elements.check_method: Compare busy and the modeled dSCL/dSDA transition events after synchronization and filter settling. Require busy=1 at the first modeled START event and busy=0 at the subsequent modeled STOP event, with no transition based solely on raw input changes before filtering.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high long enough for the synchronizer and three-sample majority filter to settle. Drive SDA low stably through the external bus so the filtered SDA changes from high to low while filtered SCL remains high; issue a START command as needed to exercise the active command sequence.
elements.expected_response: When the current filtered SDA differs from delayed SDA in the high-SCL interval as a START transition, busy becomes 1 after the registered detection update. The start_condition comparison event is observable at the corresponding filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter histories, majority outputs, and delayed filtered values. At the modeled filtered SDA high-to-low transition with filtered SCL high, compare the sampled busy output after the posedge against 1 and verify the transition occurs only after the filtered/delayed mismatch.

elements.stimulus: Begin with busy asserted from a valid filtered START. Keep filtered SCL high and filtered SDA low, then drive SDA high stably through the external bus until the filtered SDA changes from low to high while filtered SCL remains high; issue a STOP command as needed to exercise the active command sequence.
elements.expected_response: When the current filtered SDA differs from delayed SDA in the high-SCL interval as a STOP transition, busy becomes 0 after the registered detection update. The stop_condition comparison event is observable at the corresponding filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and delayed-value reference model to identify the filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high. Compare busy after the following settled posedge and require a transition to 0 coincident with that modeled mismatch.

elements.stimulus: Establish busy=1 with a valid START, then cause filtered SDA to transition while filtered SCL is low, or cause a filtered SCL/SDA difference that is not an SDA high-to-low or low-to-high transition while SCL is high. Hold the resulting bus values stable afterward.
elements.expected_response: For a filtered SCL/SDA difference that is not a START or STOP transition, busy does not change because of that comparison; it remains 1 in this setup. No START or STOP event is reported.
elements.check_method: Predict filtered and delayed values cycle by cycle and identify the non-event mismatch. Check that busy remains continuously 1 across the mismatch and that no start_condition or stop_condition probe asserts.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for the synchronizer and three-sample filter histories to become high, then drive sda_i=0 while keeping scl_i=1 for at least enough enabled clocks to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the required behavior: when filtered SDA transitions from high to low while filtered SCL is high, the controller asserts the start_condition probe for the detected START event.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge of clk, compare the start_condition probe with a reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample majority filtering, and filtered SDA edge detection; require a one-event assertion after the filtered transition.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish filtered sda_i=1 and filtered scl_i=0, then drive sda_i=0 long enough for the filtered SDA high-to-low transition while keeping scl_i=0; subsequently raise scl_i=1 without another SDA transition.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of the required behavior: because filtered SCL is low when filtered SDA transitions low, the controller does not assert start_condition.
elements.check_method: Use the same cycle-accurate synchronizer/filter reference model to identify the filtered SDA transition and verify that start_condition remains deasserted for that transition and until a qualifying filtered SDA high-to-low transition occurs while filtered SCL is high.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and scl_i held high, drive sda_i low long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to establish filtered SDA low; then drive sda_i high and hold both lines high long enough for the filtered SDA low-to-high transition to occur.
elements.expected_response: The filtered STOP condition is detected: stop_condition asserts for the sampled low-to-high SDA transition while filtered SCL is high. This is the shows=true side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample majority, and delayed filtered SDA value; compare the stop_condition probe against the model on each clock after filter settling.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and scl_i held high, drive sda_i low long enough for filtered SDA to become low, then keep sda_i low without any low-to-high transition while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: No filtered STOP condition is detected: stop_condition remains deasserted. This is the shows=false side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use the same synchronizer/filter reference model to confirm that filtered SDA has no low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high, and assert that stop_condition never pulses during the observation interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy=0, hold filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high long enough for the synchronizer/filter reference model to settle, then drive SDA low and hold it stable while SCL remains high so a filtered START condition is detected.
elements.expected_response: This is the asserting side of the observed behavior: on the registered update following start_condition, busy becomes 1 and remains asserted until a STOP condition or reset. Without the detected START transition, busy must not make this assertion.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate synchronizer/filter and filtered-edge reference model to identify start_condition, then compare busy after the corresponding clock edge against the model; assert that busy transitions 0-to-1 exactly on the registered START response.

elements.stimulus: First generate a valid filtered START with SCL high and SDA transitioning high-to-low to establish busy=1. Then hold filtered SCL high and filtered SDA low, drive SDA high, and hold it stable long enough for a filtered STOP condition to be detected.
elements.expected_response: This is the clearing side of the observed behavior: on the registered update following stop_condition, busy becomes 0 and remains deasserted until another START or reset. Without the detected STOP transition, busy must not make this deassertion.
elements.check_method: Use the cycle-accurate filter reference model to identify the START and subsequent stop_condition, then compare busy after each registered update; require busy=1 after START and an exact 1-to-0 transition after STOP.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt to a nonzero value, and keep scl_i and sda_i released high. Issue a START command on an enabled timing tick. When the START sequence releases SCL high, hold scl_i low long enough for filtered SCL to remain low, while allowing the controller's SDA transition to produce the filtered START condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of REQ-0113: bus-status detection proceeds and busy is set on the registered update for the filtered START, but cmd_ack is withheld while released-high SCL is held low. The timing counter and command phase do not advance during the stretch; after scl_i is released and filtered SCL becomes high, the command resumes and cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock at normal completion.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronizer/filter latency, slave-wait detection, counter pausing, and FSM progression. Assert busy setting occurs despite the stretch, assert no cmd_ack during the filtered-SCL-low interval, then compare the eventual one-cycle cmd_ack and phase ordering against the model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a START command with scl_i and sda_i initially high. During the command's released-SCL-high phase, externally force scl_i low to create a filtered SCL falling edge while the master remains released, then release scl_i high and allow the controller-generated SDA transition to be filtered as a START condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of REQ-0113 for multi-master synchronization: busy is set when the filtered START is detected, while cmd_ack is withheld through the external SCL falling-edge synchronization and the restarted low-period timing. The command completes only after synchronized timing permits further progress, and cmd_ack then pulses for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: Monitor the scl_sync_event and start_condition probes and compare their registered effects with a reference model. Verify busy is updated despite synchronization, verify the counter reload and absence of cmd_ack during resynchronization, and check the final one-cycle cmd_ack against modeled completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high without any clock stretching or external SCL falling edge, and issue a START command on an enabled timing tick. Allow the controller's SDA transition to produce the filtered START condition while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise side of REQ-0113: busy is set on the registered filtered START update, and cmd_ack reaches the command's normal terminal phase without an additional stall or resynchronization delay. cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: Run the same divider, synchronizer, filter, and FSM reference model with no stretch or synchronization injection. Compare busy timing and cmd_ack latency and width, and verify the normal completion latency is shorter than the corresponding stretched and resynchronized cases by the modeled delay.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 on an enabled timing tick. Drive scl_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to make filtered SCL low. Allow the WRITE sequence to reach the phase where scl_oen releases SCL high, then continue holding scl_i low.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: while scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL remains low, the internal slave_wait indication is asserted. The timing counter and bit-level FSM do not advance to the next high-phase completion state until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: Use the slave_wait probe and a reference model of the synchronizer/filter and timing FSM. At the first settled clock with scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL=0, compare slave_wait=1; while those conditions persist, verify no clk_en-driven FSM progression.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 on an enabled timing tick. Drive scl_i high and hold it long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to make filtered SCL high. Allow the WRITE sequence to reach the phase where scl_oen releases SCL high.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of the observed behavior: when scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL is high, slave_wait remains deasserted, the timing counter is not paused, and the WRITE sequence advances on subsequent clk_en ticks toward SCL low and command completion.
elements.check_method: Use the slave_wait and clk_en_tick probes with a reference model of filtered SCL and the divider. Confirm slave_wait=0 during the released-high phase and confirm that the FSM advances and eventually produces the normal command completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and hold scl_i and sda_i high until the START command is accepted. When the controller releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1) during the command sequence, drive scl_i low and keep it low long enough for synchronization and filtering to make filtered SCL remain low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: while scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL remains low, slave_wait is asserted, indicating that a slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low. The command phase does not proceed to the next high-phase step until filtered SCL is released high.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, correlate slave_wait with the condition scl_oen=1 and the reference-model filtered SCL=0; require slave_wait=1 throughout the sustained wait interval and require no command-phase advancement before filtered SCL becomes 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and hold scl_i and sda_i high until the START command is accepted. During the command phase when the controller releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), continue driving scl_i high so synchronized and filtered SCL become high.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: when SCL is released and filtered SCL is high, slave_wait remains deasserted, showing that no slave or other bus participant is holding SCL low; the command may advance according to the normal timing sequence.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, compare slave_wait against the reference-model condition scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL=1; require slave_wait=0 and verify normal command-phase advancement without a slave-wait pause.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command while the bus is high, and when the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1), externally hold scl_i low so slave_wait becomes active. Maintain scl_i low for multiple enabled clocks, then release scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: While slave_wait is active, this is the holding case of the observed behavior: cmd_ack remains low, no command-completion pulse occurs, the timing counter remains paused, and the active START FSM phase does not advance. After scl_i is released and filtered SCL becomes high, timing resumes and the START sequence eventually completes with exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the divider, filtered SCL, slave_wait, and START FSM. During every cycle with slave_wait=1, assert that no clk_en_tick occurs, the active FSM probe does not change, and cmd_ack=0; after slave_wait clears, compare phase ordering and the single terminal cmd_ack pulse against the model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command while the bus is high, and leave scl_i high whenever the controller releases SCL so slave_wait never becomes active.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of the observed behavior: the START FSM advances through its terminal phase without an SCL-stretch delay, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock at the normal command-completion boundary.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model with filtered SCL continuously high during released-SCL phases. Assert slave_wait=0, verify clk_en_tick and FSM phase progression continue, and compare the observed one-clock cmd_ack timing with the model's normal completion boundary.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, and a valid command such as START active, wait until the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1) and the filtered SCL is high. Drive scl_i high, then drive an external falling edge on scl_i while scl_oen remains 1; keep the external bus otherwise stable.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case of REQ-0117, the controller asserts scl_sync_event for the detected external filtered SCL falling edge, reloads its timing counter, and synchronizes its local low-period timing to the shared bus clock before continuing timing.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the synchronizer, filter, filtered-SCL falling-edge detector, divider, and FSM timing. At the modeled filtered falling edge while scl_oen=1, compare the scl_sync_event probe to a one-cycle assertion and verify that the modeled counter reload and subsequent low-period phase alignment match the DUT timing.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same valid-command sequence and wait until the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1) with filtered SCL high, but keep scl_i high throughout the released-SCL interval; do not introduce an external SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: For the non-holding case of REQ-0117, scl_sync_event remains deasserted, no external-edge timing-counter reload occurs, and local low-period timing follows the ordinary divider/FSM timing rather than synchronized external-clock timing.
elements.check_method: Run the same reference model with no filtered SCL falling edge while scl_oen=1. Assert that the scl_sync_event probe never pulses during the interval and compare subsequent counter-driven phase transitions against the ordinary, non-reloaded timing model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, provide a released-high bus, and issue a valid WRITE command with din=0. After command acceptance and each observed WRITE phase, apply enabled clock edges fewer than the counter interval required for the next cnt expiration, without asserting reset, ena low, clock stretching, or external SCL interference.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-expiration side of the observed behavior: scl_oen holds its current phase and does not advance toward the next WRITE phase while the internal timing interval has not expired; cmd_ack is not asserted solely because these non-expiring clocks occurred.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of cnt and compare it with sampled scl_oen after each posedge clk. Assert that scl_oen remains unchanged on enabled clocks for which the model predicts cnt has not expired, and that no premature WRITE phase transition or cmd_ack occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, provide a released-high bus, and issue a valid WRITE command with din=0. Continue applying enabled clock edges with no stalls, resets, or external SCL interference until the counter expires at successive WRITE bit-timing boundaries.
elements.expected_response: This is the transition side of the observed behavior: when cnt expires, scl_oen advances from 0 to 1 to release SCL for the WRITE high phase, then from 1 back to 0 to end that phase and advance the bit-level operation; the command eventually completes with a one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Compare the post-posedge scl_oen waveform and phase ordering against a reference model that reloads and decrements cnt from clk_cnt. Assert each expected 0-to-1 and 1-to-0 transition occurs only on the modeled expiration tick, with no missing or extra phase transitions before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Hold reset inactive, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, present cmd=START while the bus is released high with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then provide the expected external bus levels without clock stretching or synchronization events.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after START acceptance, cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock when the command reaches its terminal phase, with command phase progress occurring only after timing intervals governed by cnt loaded from clk_cnt and decremented on rising clk edges.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, record cmd_ack and the command-sequence probe states; compare the observed phase and acknowledgement timing against a reference counter initialized from clk_cnt and decremented each clock. Verify cmd_ack is a single-cycle pulse at the modeled terminal phase.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the identical START transaction and bus conditions used in TP-0000, but set clk_cnt=8 before command acceptance; keep ena=1, reset inactive, and prevent clock stretching or external SCL synchronization.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: cmd_ack must occur later than in the clk_cnt=1 transaction by the corresponding additional counter-driven timing intervals; it must not complete at the same timing as TP-0000. This demonstrates that cnt is loaded from the larger clk_cnt value and decremented on successive rising clk edges before phase advancement.
elements.check_method: Measure cycles from command acceptance to the one-cycle cmd_ack pulse and compare clk_cnt=8 against the clk_cnt=1 baseline and a reference counter model. Fail if the completion timing is unchanged or if command phases advance before the modeled counter expiry.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, present a valid START command with a released-high bus, then clock the DUT while keeping ena high. Continue through the counter reload and decrement sequence until the reference counter reaches expiration.
elements.expected_response: When the internal timing counter expires, clk_en_tick asserts for the expiration clock and the command FSM advances from its current timed phase; this is the holding case of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare the observed clk_en_tick probe and command-FSM phase transition against a reference model that reloads from clk_cnt and decrements on each enabled clock. Require exactly one asserted tick at the modeled expiration and no tick in other modeled cycles.

elements.stimulus: Using the same reset, ena=1, clk_cnt=3, released-high bus, and valid START sequence, observe the enabled countdown on each clock before the modeled expiration, without changing command or bus inputs.
elements.expected_response: While the counter remains nonzero and has not expired, clk_en_tick remains deasserted and the command FSM does not advance due to timing enable; this is the non-holding case of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference counter to identify all pre-expiration cycles and compare the clk_en_tick probe and FSM state at each posedge. Require clk_en_tick=0 and no timing-driven FSM transition until the modeled expiration cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus (scl_i=1 and sda_i=1), set clk_cnt to a value greater than 1, issue a valid WRITE command with din=1, and after the WRITE sequence reaches its stable high phase, sample several posedges before the next timing-counter expiration while keeping reset inactive and preventing arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: This is the not-held case: while clk_en is not asserted, the FSM remains in the current released-high WRITE phase and scl_oen remains 1; it does not change to 0 or otherwise advance the bit-timing phase.
elements.check_method: Use the clk_en_tick and write_stable_high_phase probes with a cycle-accurate divider/FSM reference model; on every sampled posedge where write_stable_high_phase=1 and clk_en_tick=0, assert that scl_oen remains 1 and that no phase-transition event occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus (scl_i=1 and sda_i=1), set clk_cnt to a value greater than 1, issue a valid WRITE command with din=1, and allow the command to reach its stable high phase; continue clocking until the timing counter expires and clk_en_tick asserts, with reset inactive and no arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: This is the held/advance case: when clk_en is asserted in the active stable-high WRITE phase, the FSM advances to the next bit-timing phase and scl_oen changes from 1 to 0 on the corresponding registered update, pulling SCL low.
elements.check_method: Correlate clk_en_tick, write_stable_high_phase, and scl_oen at settled posedge samples. Assert that the first qualifying clk_en_tick causes the reference-model phase transition and the registered scl_oen transition from 1 to 0, and that the transition does not occur earlier.

elements.stimulus: Reset the core, set ena=1 and a valid clk_cnt, issue a supported WRITE command with the bus available, and wait until the command has entered an active timing phase. Then drive ena=0 and hold it low for several clk cycles before restoring ena=1.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of observed_via.shows: while ena=0, scl_oen remains at the current timed FSM phase, no bit-level FSM phase transition occurs, and cmd_ack is not generated. The timing counter is reloaded while disabled, so after ena returns high the command resumes from the held phase using normal timing rather than advancing for the disabled cycles; the command eventually completes and pulses cmd_ack only after re-enablement.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen, cmd_ack, and the in_write_sequence probe after each posedge. Compare the disabled interval and post-reenable trace against a reference divider/FSM model that reloads its counter and suppresses clk_en whenever ena=0; assert no scl_oen transition or cmd_ack during the disabled interval.

elements.stimulus: Reset the core, set ena=1 and the same valid clk_cnt used in the disabled test, issue the same supported WRITE command, and keep ena=1 throughout the active command.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting otherwise side of observed_via.shows: scl_oen advances through the commanded timing phases on timing ticks and the FSM reaches command completion, producing a one-clock cmd_ack. The progression occurs without the hold imposed by ena=0.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen, cmd_ack, and the in_write_sequence and clk_en_tick probes after each posedge. Compare phase transitions and completion against the reference timing/FSM model with ena continuously high, and verify that scl_oen changes and cmd_ack occur as the active command progresses.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and provide clk_en timing ticks until the WRITE operation reaches and completes its released-SCL-high phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: while the WRITE command is in its stable released-high phase, arbitration_checking is asserted, indicating that SDA arbitration checking is performed during the WRITE operation; the command then completes normally.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered updates, use the in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and arbitration_checking probes. Assert that arbitration_checking becomes 1 during the WRITE stable-high phase and is not skipped before cmd_ack; compare the observed phase sequence against a reference FSM model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, issue cmd=READ (1000), hold scl_i and sda_i high except for a valid read sample, and provide clk_en timing ticks through the complete READ operation.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting, non-holding side: during the READ operation, arbitration_checking remains deasserted because arbitration checking is specific to WRITE operations; the READ sequence still releases SDA, samples the read bit, and completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_read_sequence and arbitration_checking after every posedge. Assert arbitration_checking=0 for the entire READ sequence and verify that it is asserted in no READ phase, using a reference model to distinguish READ phases from WRITE arbitration phases.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al cleared, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, and drive the external bus so filtered SDA remains low while the DUT releases SDA (sda_oen=1) during the WRITE stable high phase. Provide filtered SCL high and the required clk_en ticks to advance the WRITE sequence.
elements.expected_response: When write_stable_high_phase is asserted, the internal SDA arbitration check is enabled; because released-high SDA is observed low, al asserts. This is the 'al asserts' side of the observed_via REQ-0125 behavior. The command aborts without cmd_ack and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Use the write_stable_high_phase probe to identify the stable high interval and compare al against a reference FSM/arbitration model at the settled posedge. Confirm no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command and sample sda_oen/scl_oen after the abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al cleared, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, and allow the external bus to remain high so filtered SDA is high while the DUT releases SDA (sda_oen=1) during the WRITE stable high phase. Provide filtered SCL high and the required clk_en ticks to reach and complete the stable high phase.
elements.expected_response: When write_stable_high_phase is asserted, the internal SDA arbitration check is enabled; because released-high SDA is observed high, no arbitration loss is detected and al remains deasserted. This is the 'al remains deasserted' side of the observed_via REQ-0125 behavior. The WRITE sequence proceeds toward its normal completion and cmd_ack pulses once.
elements.check_method: Use the write_stable_high_phase probe to identify the stable high interval and compare al against a reference FSM/arbitration model at each settled posedge. Verify al stays low through completion and cmd_ack is a single pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, set ena=1, issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=1, and provide a released-high bus until the WRITE reaches its high phase with sda_oen=1. During that released-high arbitration-checking phase, externally drive SDA low long enough for the synchronized, three-sample filtered SDA value to become low; keep SCL in the required high phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of observed_via.shows: because the controller expects SDA high while sda_oen=1 but filtered SDA is low, al asserts on the corresponding registered clock update, the WRITE aborts without cmd_ack, and al remains asserted until reset.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization and majority filtering to identify the filtered-SDA-low arbitration window; sample al after each posedge and verify it transitions from 0 to 1 no later than the arbitration decision update, remains 1 through subsequent clocks, and that no cmd_ack is emitted for the aborted WRITE.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, set ena=1, issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=1, and keep the external SDA and SCL lines released high throughout the WRITE high phase while sda_oen=1, allowing the filtered SDA value to remain high through the arbitration-checking window.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise side of observed_via.shows: al does not assert as a result of the SDA arbitration condition, remains low, and the WRITE follows its normal completion path and produces its one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model to confirm filtered SDA remains high while sda_oen=1 and arbitration checking is active; compare registered al and cmd_ack after each posedge, requiring al to stay 0 through completion and cmd_ack to pulse exactly once.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, set ena high and issue a READ command on an enabled timing tick. During the active read sequence with filtered SCL high, drive filtered SDA low and then high for sufficient time to produce a filtered STOP condition while the command is still active.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP detection edge during the non-STOP active command, al asserts, indicating the unexpected STOP case in REQ-0126, and remains asserted until reset; this is the asserting side of the specified behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered STOP-condition probe and active-command/read-sequence probes to align the event, then sample registered al after the detecting posedge and compare against a reference model; verify al remains high on subsequent clocks without reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, set ena high and issue a STOP command on an enabled timing tick. Allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, and release SDA while filtered SCL is high so that the command's filtered STOP condition is detected while the STOP command is active.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP detection edge during the STOP command, al does not assert and remains low; this is the exempting side of the specified behavior. The STOP command completes normally with its command-complete pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the stop-sequence and filtered STOP-condition probes to identify the detection edge, then compare registered al and cmd_ack against a reference model; require al to remain low through completion and verify exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt to a nonzero value, keep the bus released-high, issue cmd=READ (1000) on an enabled timing tick, and wait until the controller is in the read sample window with filtered SCL high. Drive filtered SDA low and then high while filtered SCL remains high long enough to create an unexpected filtered STOP during the active READ command.
