elements.expected_response: The unexpected STOP causes arbitration loss; on the arbitration-loss clock edge al asserts, the FSM returns to idle, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are high, which is the 'scl_oen is high' and 'sda_oen is high' side of observed_via. The aborted command does not generate cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the in_read_sequence/read_sample_window and stop_condition probes to identify the active-command injection point; sample al, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen after each posedge. Assert that the first cycle processing the unexpected STOP has al=1, in_idle=1, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1, and that both enables remain released afterward.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt to a nonzero value, keep the bus high, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0 on an enabled timing tick, and allow the write to proceed normally. During the released-SCL high phase, keep SDA low as required for din=0 and do not inject an unexpected STOP or arbitration fault.
elements.expected_response: The normal WRITE path is the contrasting 'scl_oen does not rise high as the arbitration-loss response' and 'sda_oen does not rise high as the arbitration-loss response' side of observed_via: while the command remains active in its stable high phase, the FSM is not idle and sda_oen remains low to drive din=0, so both output enables are not released together. The command then completes normally with cmd_ack and without al.
elements.check_method: Use in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and active_command probes to sample the stable high phase after posedges. Assert in_idle=0 and al=0 during that phase, scl_oen=1 as SCL is released, and sda_oen=0 for din=0; verify that no simultaneous scl_oen=1/sda_oen=1 arbitration-loss response occurs before normal completion and cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: While the controller is idle, issue cmd=READ (1000) with ena=1 and allow the READ sequence to reach its sampling window with scl_oen released. Drive the external bus and filter-history samples so that a filtered SCL rising edge occurs while the filtered SDA value is 1; make the raw SDA history include a differing most-recent sample to ensure the check uses the filtered value.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the filtered SCL rising edge during the active READ sampling window, dout updates to 1, the value of filtered SDA, regardless of the differing raw/latest SDA sample.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample majority filtering, and filtered SCL edge detection. At the posedge that observes filtered_scl_rise and read_sample_window, compare registered dout after NBA settling with the model's filtered SDA value and require dout=1.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=READ from idle with ena=1 and reach the READ sampling window. After initializing dout to a known value, change the external SDA input so the filtered SDA changes, but hold filtered SCL low or high without producing a filtered SCL rising edge while the READ sampling window is active; do not provide the qualifying filtered SCL rise.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case: dout does not update from the changed filtered SDA value because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs in the READ sampling window; dout retains its previous registered value.
elements.check_method: Track filtered SDA and filtered SCL with the reference model, identify cycles in the READ window without filtered_scl_rise, and compare dout after each posedge against its prior value. Require no dout change attributable to filtered SDA on those cycles.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released bus, issue a READ command. Hold filtered SDA low through the filter sampling event, keep scl_oen=1, and drive scl_i high long enough for the synchronized, three-sample filtered SCL history to change its majority from low to high.
elements.expected_response: On the registered update corresponding to the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 0, the filtered SDA value sampled at that edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model and filtered_scl_rise probe to identify the rising-edge sampling event; compare dout after the posedge with the modeled filtered SDA value and verify the update occurs only at that event.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released bus, issue a READ command. Hold filtered SDA high through the filter sampling event, keep scl_oen=1, and drive scl_i high long enough for the synchronized, three-sample filtered SCL history to change its majority from low to high.
elements.expected_response: On the registered update corresponding to the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 1, the filtered SDA value sampled at that edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model and filtered_scl_rise probe to identify the rising-edge sampling event; compare dout after the posedge with the modeled filtered SDA value and verify the update occurs only at that event.

elements.stimulus: First issue a READ with filtered SDA high and allow a filtered SCL rising edge to set dout=1. Then issue another READ with ena=1, keep scl_oen=1, and hold scl_i low so filtered SCL never has a rising edge during the read sampling interval.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting no-event side of the requirement holds: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout retains its previous value of 1 and does not update.
elements.check_method: Track filtered_scl_rise with the reference filter model and assert that no event occurs during the second READ; sample dout after each posedge and compare it against its previous value, requiring it to remain 1.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ while the bus is released. During the active READ sequence, drive SDA so the filtered SDA value is 1, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge and keep the READ active until command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the filtered SCL rising edge, dout presents 1 as the received data bit for the READ operation and remains available until the READ command completes.
elements.check_method: At the posedge that processes filtered_scl_rise while in_read_sequence, compare dout with the reference model's filtered SDA value. Confirm the value is observable before cmd_ack and record a received-bit bin for value 1.

elements.stimulus: Preset dout to a known value, set ena=1, and issue cmd=READ. Keep the controller in the READ sequence before the filtered SCL rising-edge sampling point; do not produce a filtered SCL rising edge, then observe dout during this pre-sampling interval.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because no filtered SCL rising edge has occurred during the active READ sequence, dout does not indicate a new READ received bit; it may retain its previous value. No received-bit update is reported before the sampling edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the interval before filtered_scl_rise. Assert that dout has no new READ capture event or value transition attributable to this READ operation, while allowing the previously stored dout value to remain unchanged.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive cmd=START (4'b0001), and choose a nonzero clk_cnt large enough that no clk_en_tick occurs for several rising edges. Hold cmd and the bus inputs stable during those edges.
elements.expected_response: This is the side of shows where the requirement holds: in_idle remains asserted on every sampled clock while the valid command is available but clk_en_tick is 0; no command phase begins and no command-complete pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, assert the in_idle probe is 1 and verify no start-sequence probe activation or cmd_ack pulse occurs before the reference divider predicts clk_en_tick.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive cmd=START (4'b0001), hold it stable, and wait until the reference divider produces clk_en_tick while the FSM is idle.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting side of shows where the requirement no longer holds: on the enabled timing tick, the FSM leaves idle and enters the START command sequence, observable as in_idle deasserting and in_start_sequence asserting on the resulting registered state.
elements.check_method: Use a divider reference model to identify the first clk_en_tick with cmd=START and ena=1; sample probes after that posedge and require in_idle=0 with the START sequence active, without requiring a fixed wall-clock latency.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, deassert reset, wait for in_idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present cmd=4'b0001 (START), and hold the command through the next enabled timing tick with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the idle decoder selects START. After command acceptance, sda_oen remains released initially, then drives SDA low while SCL is high, and the START sequence completes without selecting a STOP, READ, WRITE, or no-operation signature.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after NBA settling, compare the sda_oen trace against the reference START signature and verify the command FSM probe transitions from in_idle to in_start_sequence and then returns to in_idle.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue and complete a START command to establish a busy transaction, wait for in_idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present cmd=4'b0010 (STOP), and hold the command through the next enabled timing tick with scl_i=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the idle decoder selects STOP. sda_oen drives SDA low first and later releases SDA while SCL is high; the STOP signature is produced and no START, READ, WRITE, or no-operation signature is selected.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered sda_oen waveform with the reference STOP sequence and verify in_stop_sequence is entered after acceptance and the FSM subsequently returns to in_idle.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, wait for in_idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present cmd=4'b1000 (READ), hold it through the next enabled timing tick, and provide scl_i and sda_i high initially, then a filtered SCL rising edge during the read window.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the idle decoder selects READ. sda_oen remains released throughout the read operation so the external device can drive SDA; no SDA drive-low phase characteristic of START, STOP, or WRITE occurs.
elements.check_method: Compare sda_oen against the reference READ trace, verify in_read_sequence and read_sample_window are asserted, and verify the trace is not the idle no-operation trace because a read sequence and its completion event occur.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, wait for in_idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, present cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE), and hold the command through the next enabled timing tick with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the idle decoder selects WRITE. sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, then releases SCL for the write high phase while retaining the WRITE-specific SDA behavior; no START, STOP, READ, or no-operation signature is selected.
elements.check_method: Compare sda_oen at every registered phase with the reference WRITE(din=0) signature and verify in_write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase are entered before returning to in_idle.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, wait for in_idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present cmd=4'b0000 (NOP), and hold it through multiple enabled timing ticks with both bus lines released high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for no operation: sda_oen remains in the idle released state for the entire observation interval; no command sequence is started and no command-specific SDA waveform occurs.
elements.check_method: Sample sda_oen after each posedge and verify it remains at the idle released value, in_idle stays asserted, and no command-sequence probe becomes active.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, wait for in_idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present unsupported cmd=4'b0011, and hold it through multiple enabled timing ticks with both bus lines released high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the unsupported command must not select any START, STOP, READ, or WRITE signature. sda_oen remains in the idle released state and the FSM remains idle rather than producing a command sequence.
elements.check_method: Compare the sda_oen waveform against each supported-command signature and verify it remains idle-released while in_idle stays asserted and in_start_sequence, in_stop_sequence, in_read_sequence, and in_write_sequence never assert.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, set ena=1, drive cmd=START (4'b0001), and hold it through the next clk_en_tick while in_idle is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled command-acceptance tick, the FSM leaves in_idle and enters in_start_sequence.
elements.check_method: At the clk_en_tick and after registered state updates settle, sample in_idle and in_start_sequence; require in_idle=0 and in_start_sequence=1, with no transition into any other command-sequence probe.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, set ena=1, drive cmd=STOP (4'b0010), and hold it through the next clk_en_tick while in_idle is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled command-acceptance tick, the FSM leaves in_idle and enters in_stop_sequence.
elements.check_method: At the clk_en_tick and after registered state updates settle, sample in_idle and in_stop_sequence; require in_idle=0 and in_stop_sequence=1, with no transition into any other command-sequence probe.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, set ena=1, drive cmd=READ (4'b1000), and hold it through the next clk_en_tick while in_idle is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled command-acceptance tick, the FSM leaves in_idle and enters in_read_sequence.
elements.check_method: At the clk_en_tick and after registered state updates settle, sample in_idle and in_read_sequence; require in_idle=0 and in_read_sequence=1, with no transition into any other command-sequence probe.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, set ena=1, drive cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), and hold it through the next clk_en_tick while in_idle is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled command-acceptance tick, the FSM leaves in_idle and enters in_write_sequence.
elements.check_method: At the clk_en_tick and after registered state updates settle, sample in_idle and in_write_sequence; require in_idle=0 and in_write_sequence=1, with no transition into any other command-sequence probe.

elements.stimulus: For each command value cmd=4'b0000, 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, and 4'b1111, reset or otherwise return the DUT to idle, set ena=1, drive the value through the next clk_en_tick, and then hold it for one additional clock.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: for NOP and every unsupported command value, the FSM remains in_idle; it does not enter in_start_sequence, in_stop_sequence, in_read_sequence, or in_write_sequence.
elements.check_method: For every enumerated cmd value, sample all five FSM probes after the enabled clk_en_tick and after the additional clock; require in_idle=1 continuously and all four command-sequence probes=0, with no command-sequence transition observed.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive cmd=START (4'b0001) on an enabled clk_en acceptance opportunity, keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 so the bus is released high, and continue clocking until the START sequence reaches its SDA-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the START sequence, scl_oen becomes 1 to release SCL; sda_oen is initially 1 to release SDA and then becomes 0 while scl_oen remains 1, producing SDA low while SCL remains released high. This is the required side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use a scoreboard or temporal assertion on registered outputs after each posedge: observe the ordered sequence sda_oen=1 and scl_oen=1, followed by sda_oen=0 with scl_oen=1, without an intervening scl_oen=0; mark the START-sequence bin and fail if the order or SCL release condition is violated.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and issue NOP (4'b0000) while scl_i=1 and sda_i=1; clock for at least the number of enabled timing ticks needed to reach the corresponding interval used by TP-0000, without issuing START.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because no START command is activated, sda_oen must not exhibit the required release-then-low transition while scl_oen remains 1; the controller remains in its idle output behavior and must not create an SDA-low START phase. This is the negative side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and sda_oen over the complete stimulus window and assert that no interval exists with the START transition pattern sda_oen=1 followed later by sda_oen=0 while scl_oen remains 1; also check that no START-sequence probe activation occurs.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue cmd=4'b0001 (START) while in_idle is asserted. Allow the START sequence to generate the filtered SDA-high-to-low transition while SCL is high, then continue enabled clocks through the terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0135: after the START condition, scl_oen becomes low, the command FSM returns to idle, and cmd_ack becomes high for exactly one clock cycle. cmd_ack is low on the following clock and no additional completion pulse occurs.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge, use the in_start_sequence and in_idle probes to identify the START terminal phase and completion. Assert scl_oen=0 and in_idle=1 when completion occurs; measure cmd_ack high duration with a consecutive-cycle assertion of one cycle followed by cmd_ack=0.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and issue cmd=4'b0001 (START). Once the filtered START condition is observed while the FSM is still in the START sequence, assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the terminal SCL-low/completion phase, then release nReset without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0135: the completion behavior is aborted; scl_oen is not low but is reset to released high, cmd_ack remains low with no one-clock completion pulse, and the FSM is idle due to reset.
elements.check_method: Observe outputs immediately after nReset assertion and on subsequent settled posedges. Check scl_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, and in_idle=1; assert that no cmd_ack rising pulse occurs from the aborted START after reset release.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 to represent an idle released bus. Set ena=1, cmd=0010 (STOP), and hold the command until it is accepted on an enabled timing tick. Continue clocking until cmd_ack asserts.
elements.expected_response: The holding case of REQ-0136 is observed: during the STOP sequence, sda_oen first becomes 0 while SDA is driven low; scl_oen then becomes 1 while sda_oen remains 0, releasing SCL; finally sda_oen becomes 1 while scl_oen remains 1, releasing SDA to generate STOP. The sequence completes with a one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use a temporal scoreboard sampled after each posedge: assert that the first STOP-phase SDA ownership is sda_oen=0, that a later phase has scl_oen=1 before any final SDA release, and that the first sda_oen=1 after the low phase occurs only while scl_oen=1. Also check cmd_ack is a single-cycle pulse after the ordered phases.

elements.stimulus: After reset with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set ena=1 and issue cmd=0001 (START) on an enabled timing tick. Continue clocking through completion, without issuing a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting non-holding case is observed: sda_oen may become 0 to create the START condition, but the port sequence must not show the REQ-0136 STOP ordering of SDA release after SCL release. In particular, there must be no final transition sda_oen=0 to sda_oen=1 while scl_oen remains 1 as a STOP condition; the START sequence instead pulls SCL low after SDA is pulled low.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and sda_oen with a command-qualified trace assertion. For the START command, fail if the trace contains the STOP signature: sda_oen=0, followed by scl_oen=1, followed by sda_oen=1 before SCL is pulled low. Compare the observed trace against the positive STOP signature from TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=0010 (STOP), and provide a released-high bus so the STOP sequence can complete. Wait through the sequence until SCL is released high and SDA is released high, then observe the completion edge and the following clock.
elements.expected_response: When the STOP completion phase is reached, the FSM is in idle and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock; cmd_ack is low on the following clock. This is the holding case of the observed behavior: the port pulses cmd_ack when the requirement holds.
elements.check_method: Use the in_stop_sequence and in_idle probes to identify the sequence and completion transition. At the completion edge compare cmd_ack=1 and in_idle=1, then assert cmd_ack=0 on the next sampled clock; count exactly one high cycle.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue cmd=0010 (STOP) with a released-high bus. Allow the STOP sequence to reach its final completion phase, then assert synchronous rst=1 on the clock at which completion would otherwise occur.
elements.expected_response: Reset aborts the STOP sequence and returns the FSM to idle, but cmd_ack remains low at the attempted STOP completion edge and does not produce a one-clock pulse. This is the otherwise case of the observed behavior: the port remains low when the requirement does not hold because completion was aborted.
elements.check_method: Sample after the reset clock's nonblocking updates. Check in_idle=1, cmd_ack=0 at the attempted completion edge, and cmd_ack=0 on subsequent clocks until a new valid command completes; verify no cmd_ack high pulse occurred.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while the FSM is idle; provide a released-high bus and allow the enabled timing ticks to advance the command into its data-bit phase, keeping al=0 and resets inactive until completion.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of REQ-0138: during the READ data-bit phase, while in_read_sequence is asserted and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, so SDA is released for the external slave to drive.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge while in_read_sequence/read_sample_window is asserted, compare sda_oen against 1'b1; verify the observation occurs after READ acceptance and before the command-complete pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=0 while the FSM is idle; provide a released-high bus and allow the enabled timing ticks to advance into the WRITE data-bit phase, keeping al=0 and resets inactive.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting, non-holding case of REQ-0138: outside the READ data-bit phase, during the WRITE data-bit phase with din=0, sda_oen is 0 and the controller drives SDA low rather than releasing it.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge while in_write_sequence is asserted before the SCL release/high phase, compare sda_oen against 1'b0 and confirm in_read_sequence is 0; distinguish this value from the sda_oen=1 observation required in TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: With the FSM idle and the bus externally released high, set ena=1 and cmd=1000 (READ) before an enabled timing tick. Keep scl_i and sda_i high, allow the READ command to enter in_read_sequence and read_sample_window, then provide the filtered SCL rising edge and continue until the READ low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of observed_via.shows: during the READ read window, scl_oen is 1, releasing SCL high; after the read window and its filtered SCL rising edge, scl_oen becomes 0 for the subsequent SCL-low phase.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block monitor sampled after each posedge and correlate scl_oen with in_read_sequence, read_sample_window, filtered_scl_rise, and the subsequent low-phase state. Compare the observed phase ordering against a divider/filter/FSM reference model and require no premature scl_oen=0 during the read window.

elements.stimulus: With the FSM idle and the bus externally released high, set ena=1 and cmd=1000 (READ), wait until read_sample_window is active with scl_oen=1, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the filtered SCL rising edge or the normal transition to the SCL-low phase; release nReset afterward.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case of observed_via.shows: reset aborts the READ sequence, asynchronously returns the controller to its reset/idle condition, and releases SCL with scl_oen=1; there is no READ-window-to-subsequent-low-phase transition in this aborted operation, so scl_oen must not be credited as satisfying the normal hold-then-pull-low behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen asynchronously at nReset assertion and on subsequent settled clock edges, while checking in_idle and reset state. Confirm the active READ sequence terminates without reaching its normal SCL-low phase and distinguish this reset-aborted observation from the normal behavior using the reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue the READ command on a clk_en tick, keep the external bus released, drive SDA high long enough for the filter to produce filtered SDA=1, then drive SCL high long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL signal to transition low-to-high. Observe filtered_scl_rise at the resulting clock edge.
elements.expected_response: On the edge where filtered_scl_rise indicates the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 1, the filtered SDA value captured at that edge. This is the positive side of the observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronizers, filter histories, majority filtering, and filtered edge detection. At each settled posedge, when the model and filtered_scl_rise probe indicate the rising edge, compare dout with the model's filtered SDA value and require dout=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue the READ command on a clk_en tick, hold the external SCL line low so filtered SCL never transitions from low to high, and toggle or change SDA sufficiently for filtered SDA to change while SCL remains low. Initialize dout to 0 and wait through multiple enabled filter-sampling intervals without producing filtered_scl_rise.
elements.expected_response: Because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout does not update from a filtered SDA capture and remains 0. This is the negative side of the observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that filtered_scl_rise remains deasserted throughout the observation window. Compare dout after every settled posedge against its pre-window value and require no dout update attributable to SDA changes without a filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted and ena high, issue cmd=READ (1000) on an enabled timing tick. Let the controller enter the READ sequence, drive a stable external SDA value, allow filtered SCL to rise for the READ sampling edge, then allow the READ low phase and subsequent enabled timing advance to complete the bit cycle.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the READ bit cycle completes, in_idle is asserted and cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock; cmd_ack then returns low while the FSM remains idle.
elements.check_method: Use the clocked reference model for command-phase advancement, synchronizer/filter latency, and filtered SCL rising-edge capture. At each posedge after the terminal READ phase, compare in_idle and cmd_ack with the model, requiring the idle transition and exactly one-cycle cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted and ena high, issue cmd=READ (1000) on an enabled timing tick and allow the controller to enter the READ sequence, but hold the external SCL line low after SCL is released so the filtered SCL rising sampling edge or the terminal READ phase cannot occur.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: while the READ bit cycle is incomplete, cmd_ack is not asserted and in_idle is not asserted after the command has been accepted; the controller remains in the active READ operation rather than indicating command completion.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_read_sequence, in_idle, and cmd_ack on settled posedge samples. Confirm the reference model identifies the READ cycle as incomplete due to held-low filtered SCL, and compare that no completion pulse or return-to-idle indication occurs until the cycle is subsequently allowed to complete.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, cmd=WRITE (0100), din=0, clk_cnt=1, and keep the external SDA and SCL lines released high. Apply clocks until the WRITE command is accepted and the FSM enters the WRITE bit phase, before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE bit phase in which SDA is set from din, sda_oen is 0. This is the holding side of the observed behavior: din=0 causes SDA to be driven low. The contrasting behavior is not expected in this scenario; sda_oen=1 for din=0 would violate the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge while in_write_sequence is asserted and before cmd_ack, compare the registered sda_oen output with din=0; require sda_oen==0 and record a bin for the din=0 case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, cmd=WRITE (0100), din=1, clk_cnt=1, and keep the external SDA and SCL lines released high. Apply clocks until the WRITE command is accepted and the FSM enters the WRITE bit phase, before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE bit phase in which SDA is set from din, sda_oen is 1. This is the contrasting side of the observed behavior: din=1 causes SDA to be released high. The opposing behavior is not expected in this scenario; sda_oen=0 for din=1 would violate the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge while in_write_sequence is asserted and before cmd_ack, compare the registered sda_oen output with din=1; require sda_oen==1 and record a bin for the din=1 case.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high, rst low, ena high, and provide a released-high bus with scl_i and sda_i high. Issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=0 on an enabled timing tick, then keep the command active without asserting reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE bit's SDA-setting and stable-high phase before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0, so the DUT drives SDA low. This is the din=0 side of the specified behavior.
elements.check_method: At every registered phase transition, sample sda_oen after the posedge and use the in_write_sequence or write_stable_high_phase probe to identify the SDA-setting and stable-high interval; assert sda_oen==0 throughout that interval until the command completes.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high, rst low, ena high, and provide a released-high bus with scl_i and sda_i high. Issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=1 on an enabled timing tick, then keep the command active without asserting reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE bit's SDA-setting and stable-high phase before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, so the DUT releases SDA high. This is the din=1 side of the specified behavior and the opposite sda_oen value from the din=0 case.
elements.check_method: At every registered phase transition, sample sda_oen after the posedge and use the in_write_sequence or write_stable_high_phase probe to identify the SDA-setting and stable-high interval; assert sda_oen==1 throughout that interval until the command completes.

elements.stimulus: After reset has established idle, set ena=1, present cmd=0100 (WRITE) on an enabled timing tick with din=1, hold scl_i and sda_i high so the released bus is not stretching or causing arbitration loss, and continue clocking until command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: during in_write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase, scl_oen becomes 1 to release SCL; in the following WRITE phase scl_oen becomes 0 to pull SCL low; the FSM reaches in_idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at completion.
elements.check_method: Use a scoreboard synchronized to posedge clk and sample after registered updates. Correlate the in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and in_idle probes with scl_oen. Assert the ordered scl_oen sequence 1 then 0, followed by idle and a single-cycle cmd_ack pulse; assert cmd_ack is low on adjacent clocks.

elements.stimulus: After reset has established idle, set ena=1 and present cmd=0000 (NOP) for an enabled timing tick while keeping scl_i and sda_i high; continue clocking for at least the duration of a complete WRITE sequence.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case of shows: because no WRITE sequence is entered, scl_oen does not exhibit the required released-high-then-driven-low WRITE sequence; it remains in the idle released state at 1, and cmd_ack remains low with no completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle and in_write_sequence after each posedge. Assert in_write_sequence never asserts, scl_oen remains 1 throughout the observation window, and cmd_ack remains 0; flag any WRITE-like scl_oen transition or acknowledgement as a failure.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported START command with cmd=0001. Provide a released-high bus and allow the command to advance through its SDA-low-while-SCL-high and subsequent SCL-low phases until cmd_ack is asserted or the command is aborted.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: throughout the command, scl_o and sda_o remain constant at 0. At the active-low drive phases, scl_oen=0 when SCL is pulled low and sda_oen=0 when SDA is pulled low; the corresponding line is driven low rather than driven high.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from command acceptance through cmd_ack or abort, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. Correlate each observed low output-enable value with the corresponding START phase and verify the modeled open-drain bus line is low whenever that enable is 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported START command with cmd=0001. Provide a released-high bus and allow the command to advance through its initial SDA/SCL release phase and later SCL-low phase until cmd_ack is asserted or the command is aborted.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting release side of shows: scl_o and sda_o still remain constant at 0, while scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 during phases where the respective SCL or SDA line is released. Neither output port drives a logic-high value; the external pulled-up bus may remain high.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from command acceptance through cmd_ack or abort, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. Identify release phases from the reference START-state model and assert the corresponding output enable is 1 and the externally modeled line is high only when no participant drives it low. Fail if either constant-low output changes or if an enable polarity is inverted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, provide a released-high bus, and issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 from idle. Allow the command to progress through its SDA-low phase, released-SCL high phase, and subsequent SCL-low phase until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: throughout the active WRITE sequence, scl_o and sda_o remain 0 at every clock edge. During the SDA-low and SCL-low drive phases, the corresponding output enable is 0, selecting active-low pull-down; during any released phase, the corresponding output enable is 1. The driven bus lines are low whenever their enable is 0.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against a command-phase reference model. Independently model each open-drain line as low when its DUT enable is 0 and high otherwise, and assert that every enable-0 phase produces a low line.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, provide a released-high bus, issue a supported START command and wait for cmd_ack, then issue a supported STOP command. Observe the initial START released phase and the final STOP phase after SCL is released and SDA is released.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting released case: during phases where the corresponding I2C line is released, scl_oen and/or sda_oen are 1, so the external bus remains high when no external device pulls it low. The constant-drive outputs scl_o and sda_o nevertheless remain 0 at every clock edge; they must never become high or act as the drive control.
elements.check_method: Use a phase-aware reference model to identify each released SCL and SDA interval, then assert the corresponding output enable is 1 and the modeled open-drain line is high with the external bus released. At all sampled edges also assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0, and flag any enable polarity inversion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena high and provide a released-high bus. On enabled timing ticks, drive the sequence through the START SDA-drive phase where sda_oen becomes 0 while scl_oen remains 1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for sda_oen: while sda_oen is 0, sda_o is 0, showing that SDA is driven low. In the same phase scl_o remains 0 while scl_oen is 1, as the constant-low output does not discriminate release from drive.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge while the START SDA-drive phase is indicated by sda_oen=0, compare sda_o==0 and record the sda_oen=0 observation; also compare scl_o==0 with scl_oen=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena high and provide a released-high bus. Continue the command until the START sequence pulls SCL low, where scl_oen becomes 0; then allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for scl_oen: while scl_oen is 0, scl_o is 0, showing that SCL is driven low. If sda_oen is also 0 during the preceding or overlapping low-drive phase, sda_o remains 0 as well.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge while scl_oen=0 during the START sequence, compare scl_o==0; if sda_oen=0 is observed, independently compare sda_o==0.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset and leave the controller idle with no command active, so both output-enable controls are high: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: with scl_oen high, scl_o remains 0, and with sda_oen high, sda_o remains 0. These outputs remain low even when the corresponding enable is not low, so the ports alone do not discriminate the enabled-drive condition.
elements.check_method: After reset settles, sample scl_oen, sda_oen, scl_o, and sda_o at settled clock boundaries and compare the observed pairs against scl_oen=1,scl_o=0 and sda_oen=1,sda_o=0.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and a released-high bus, issue a START command and observe the initial START phase in which both SCL and SDA are released.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SCL: scl_oen is high, so SCL is released and the external pull-up brings the SCL line high; scl_o remains 0.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge while the initial START phase is active, assert scl_oen==1 and sample the modeled open-drain SCL line with no external low drive; compare that the line is high.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and a released-high bus, issue a START command and advance through the phase where the controller pulls SDA low while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SCL: scl_oen is high, so SCL remains released and is brought high by the external pull-up; scl_oen is not low and the SCL line must not be driven low by the DUT.
elements.check_method: During the SDA-low/SCL-high START phase, sample scl_oen and the modeled SCL line after every posedge; require scl_oen==1 and SCL==1 with no external low drive, while confirming scl_o==0.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and a released-high bus, issue a READ command and advance until the read sample window in which SDA is released.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SDA: sda_oen is high, so SDA is released and the external pull-up brings the SDA line high when no external device drives it low; sda_o remains 0.
elements.check_method: During the read sample window, apply no external SDA low drive and sample after each settled posedge; assert sda_oen==1 and modeled SDA==1.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and a released-high bus, issue a WRITE command with din=0 and advance to the WRITE data phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SDA: sda_oen is low, indicating that the controller drives SDA low rather than releasing it; the modeled SDA line is low despite the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: During the WRITE data phase, sample after each settled posedge and assert sda_oen==0 and modeled SDA==0, with sda_o==0; verify the line is low with no external participant required.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, hold filtered bus lines released-high, and issue cmd=START while the FSM is idle. Allow the START sequence to run to its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the START terminal completion edge, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle, is low on the preceding cycle, and returns low on the immediately following cycle.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to identify START acceptance and terminal completion; sample cmd_ack after each posedge and assert one and only one high sample at completion with low samples before and after.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish a busy bus state as needed, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, and issue cmd=STOP while the FSM is idle. Allow the STOP sequence to complete with SCL released high before SDA is released.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack is asserted at the end of the STOP sequence for exactly one clk cycle and is low on both adjacent clk cycles.
elements.check_method: Model the STOP output-enable phases and terminal edge, then compare the sampled cmd_ack waveform against a single-cycle pulse aligned to that edge; flag any early, late, repeated, or extended assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, release SDA, and issue cmd=READ while idle. Drive a stable external SDA value and provide the SCL high/read window followed by SCL low so the READ sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the filtered SCL rising-edge sample and subsequent READ low phase, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle at sequence completion, then returns low.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for filtered SCL timing and READ completion; verify cmd_ack is low before the modeled terminal edge, high on exactly that completion cycle, and low on the next cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, drive din=0, release the external SDA/SCL lines, and issue cmd=WRITE while idle. Allow the WRITE sequence through its released-SCL high phase and final SCL-low phase without arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack is asserted at the end of the WRITE sequence for exactly one clk cycle, with no cmd_ack before completion and cmd_ack low again on the following clk.
elements.check_method: Track the WRITE FSM and terminal phase with the reference model; compare cmd_ack at successive posedges and require a single-cycle pulse exactly at normal sequence completion.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid WRITE command, then assert nReset asynchronously before the WRITE reaches its terminal completion phase and hold reset through the next clock edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the WRITE sequence is aborted rather than completed; cmd_ack must not assert as a completion pulse for that sequence, and it must remain low after reset is applied.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack asynchronously and on every posedge from command acceptance through reset release; require no high pulse attributable to the aborted sequence and compare reset behavior with the reference model.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue cmd=START while the filtered bus is idle with SCL and SDA high. Drive clocks and external lines so the START sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the clock edge immediately following the START terminal phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle, then returns low so the next bit command can be issued.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify the START terminal phase; sample cmd_ack after each posedge and require exactly one high sample on the immediately following clock, with low before that boundary and on the subsequent clock.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP while the bus is busy. Drive the external SCL line high after the controller releases it and allow the STOP sequence to reach its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the clock edge immediately following the STOP terminal phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle and is low on every other clock.
elements.check_method: Track the STOP sequence with a cycle-accurate reference model, identify its terminal phase, and compare the sampled cmd_ack waveform against one high cycle exactly at the completion boundary.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ. Release SDA externally or drive it to a stable sampled value, allow the READ sequence to complete its SCL high sampling window and subsequent low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the clock edge immediately following the READ terminal phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle and then deasserts.
elements.check_method: Use the modeled filtered-SCL timing and READ state progression to determine the terminal phase; assert that cmd_ack is high for one and only one following clock and remains low thereafter.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, drive din to either 0 and then 1 in separate trials, issue cmd=WRITE for each trial, and provide a released-high SCL bus without arbitration loss until the WRITE sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: for each WRITE trial, cmd_ack asserts on the clock edge immediately following the terminal phase for exactly one clock cycle, then returns low.
elements.check_method: Determine each WRITE terminal phase from the reference model and compare the registered cmd_ack waveform, requiring one high cycle at the specified boundary and no additional high cycles.

elements.stimulus: Issue each valid command type in separate trials, but observe cmd_ack from command acceptance through the active sequence and for at least two clocks after completion; also issue a valid command and hold ena=0 before its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: cmd_ack is absent before the command's terminal phase, is not held high for more than one clock, and is absent after the one-clock completion window. When ena=0 prevents the sequence from reaching its terminal phase, cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Compare the sampled cmd_ack waveform with reference-model terminal boundaries: require low on all pre-terminal and post-window cycles, exactly one high completion cycle only when a terminal phase is reached, and no pulse during the ena-disabled hold.

The check for this requirement decided NOTHING on every testpoint it already names, and this is the account it gave: the invariant held for every row seen, but the window opening at edge 9 ran to the end of trace without closing. That sentence is the target. Stage what the CHECK says it did not see, which is not always what the activation above describes.
This scenario needs RESET ASSERTED, which is not a drivable input -- the runtime owns reset on both sides at once. Use a reset step: {"reset": true} (or {"reset": true, "hold": N} to hold it N edges), then the steps that observe what reset left behind. Do not try to drive rst or nReset as a value; the schema has no such input and the step will be rejected.
This design has MORE THAN ONE RESET PORT (nReset, rst), and {"reset": true} asserts all of them at the same edge -- so a requirement about what ONE reset does can never be observed that way, because the other is asserted too. Use the port-list form {"reset": ["rst"], "hold": N}, which asserts only rst and leaves nReset at its idle value.
This scenario needs ARBITRATION LOST, which needs a second bus master -- emulate one. Drive the transfer, use {"until": {"port": "sda_oen", "value": 1}} to wait until the controller has RELEASED SDA, then in the next step drive sda_i=0 while it is still released. The controller reads back a low it did not drive, which is exactly the condition. Do not expect al to move without that contention: nothing else in a single-master sequence produces it.
It applies when these inputs hold: rst=1
